Electrodynamic systems of such oscillators are based on 2D periodical slow-wave structures realizing 2D distributed feedback mechanism, allowing for provision of stable narrow-band oscillation regime under conditions of substantial oversize. In the proof-of-principal experiments at the Ka-band under the transverse oversize (perimeter) of ~ 16 wavelength, narrow-band generation was obtained with ~ 0.2 - 0.3 MW output power level. Project to advance this oscillator into W-band with the oversized parameter of ~ 30 is in progress.

articleTitle: Blockage Impact of Human Locomotion Gaits on Terahertz Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The study targets human locomotion gait for analyzing the blockage impact on terahertz (THz) wireless links. A 3D human model 6 m from the transmitter (TX) is thus employed to impose blockage in a line-of-sight (LoS) environment with vertically polarized horn antennas possessing divergent beams. Being in motion, the channels are captured by the receivers (RX) at 9 m and 12 m. Both the TX and RX antennas possess a gain of 25.45 dBi at 300 GHz. The blockage provoked by different phases in the total walking cycle (i.e., start position, swing phase, and step) is investigated with the help of ray-tracing simulations. Moreover, keeping in account the beam spot size a walking path of 1 m and 2 m are considered in the study. The results bring out into open that the blockage effect is partially greater when the human is moving in contrast to static phases.

articleTitle: The ECRH System at W7-X: Status, Results and Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An overview is given of the development of the Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) system on the Stellarator W7-X, the results of the W7-X experimental campaigns and the planning for an upgrade of the ECRH system. In general, the perspectives for the development of future ECRH systems are presented.

articleTitle: Design and Sensitivity Analysis of an Electro-Optical System for a Ka-Band Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A pencil beam electro-optical system (EOS) for a Ka-band traveling wave tube is designed in this paper. The operating voltage and current of the electron gun are 12060 V and 0.102 A, respectively. A periodic permanent magnet (PPM) beam focusing system is designed to focus the beam and ensure a good beam transparency. The particle tracking simulation results show the beam transparency is 100% in a beam tunnel with a radius of 0.45 mm. The sensitivity of the designed EOS is investigated by varying the density and the position of the magnetic field. The simulation results show that the designed EOS can keep a beam transparency higher than 93% with slight fabrication errors.

articleTitle: Tracking Electron & Hole Dynamics in 3D Dirac Semimetals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Using ultrafast optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy (OPTP) and ultrafast terahertz emission spectroscopy, we showcase the electron and hole dynamics in Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>As<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanowires (NWs), a well-known 3D Dirac semimetal a subgroup of the newly discovered. A temperature-dependent photoconductivity measurement was carried out yielding an incredibly high electron mobility ~ 16,000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs at 5K. Strong THz emission due to helicity-dependent surface photocurrents was also observed for both nanowires and single crystal (SC) which is highly desirable for devices such as THz sources.

articleTitle: Shadow Features of Moving Targets Based on W-band SAR
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Video synthetic aperture radar (ViSAR) is regarded as an effective sensor to monitor moving targets continuously. In addition to realize video imaging, W-band radar’s high scattering characteristics on smooth roads create conditions for the formation of shadows for moving targets. This paper reports the video imaging results of an UAV borne W-band SAR on urban intersection and analyzes the shadows of moving targets. A simple speed estimation method is proposed based on the shadow model.

articleTitle: Aspects of Signal Processing for Multistatic Terahertz Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Applications of multistatic sensor arrays, which operate in the terahertz-region, are increasingly gaining importance for non-destructive testing purposes. Continuous enhancements in processing capabilities of CPUs and GPUs allow to generate volumetric images with superior speeds compared to alternative raster-scan systems. However, this requires efficient reconstruction- and correction algorithms. In addition to the system design, the choice of signal processing methods has a decisive influence on the resolution, image quality and measurement duration. In this contribution, we discuss some aspects of this signal processing along with specific examples.

articleTitle: THz-TDS Parameter Extraction via Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy is a powerful analytical technique for investigating a wide range of material samples, however calculating refractive index values is not a trivial process and can be computationally intensive. Here we investigate the use of machine learning to simplify and replace certain aspects of THz TDS data analysis. We train a neural net to convert THz TDS data into complex refractive index values by creating a large training set based on simulated data. The resultant neural net is computationally efficient and extracts TDS parameters with a high degree of accuracy. Further, we propose that by investigating the trained network we may gain new insights into THz parameter extraction procedures.

articleTitle: 0.32 THz Extended interaction Oscillator (EIO) by using TM31 mode
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A compact extended interaction oscillator (EIO) working in the THz band have been designed. The aim is to design a stable operation oscillator working at higher order TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf>-mode that can alleviate power limitation problem and high machining tolerance requirement of the conventional THz EIO operating at fundamental TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>-mode. The final design consists of a seven gaps slow-wave-structure (SWS) with transverse mode being TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> and axial mode being 2π-mode. The designed operating frequency is set at ~320 GHz. At such a high frequency, the electromagnetic losses due to skin effect and surface roughness become significant. The background material conductivity is taken to be 1.1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> (S/m). This reduced conductivity account for the electromagnetic energy losses at THz frequency. The beam-wave interaction study using PIC predicted a stable output power of 1.58 kW and interaction efficiency of 10.7%.

articleTitle: Effect of Grating Thermal Expansion on the THz Clinotron Operation
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The results of the theoretical study of the influence of grating thermal expansion on the clinotron radiation frequency has been presented and compared with the experimental data. The external system controlling a chiller for the clinotron grating temperature stability has been developed and tested. The experimental study showed the effective tuning and control of the operating frequency of the Clinotron tubes by varying the cooling water temperature.

articleTitle: Investigation of spectral encoding with terahertz broadband uniformly topologically charged beams
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a spectral binary encoding technique with broadband terahertz pulses represented as interference field of uniformly topologically charged Laguerre-Gaussian terahertz beams carrying unitary and zero topological charges. The principles of the technique and the results of investigation of its possibilities are presented.

articleTitle: Formation of Short Microwave Pulses by Laser-Driven GaAs Switch with Sub-Nanosecond Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Formation of sub-nanosecond and nanosecond scale microwave pulses from CW 170 GHz BWO has been experimentally demonstrated using quasi-optical GaAs switch with photoconductivity induced by both femtosecond 800 nm and picosecond 532 nm lasers. It has been shown that full duration at half maximum of the microwave pulses can be controlled by the energy of laser pulses in the range from sub-ns to a few nanoseconds.

articleTitle: Terahertz and Infrared Absorption Spectra of Mouse Blood Plasma in Glioma Development
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Early diagnosis of glioma may be achieved by detecting the molecular biomarkers in brain tissues and body fluids. Terahertz (THz) and infrared (IR) absorption spectra of mouse blood plasma were studied in the dynamics of the U87 glioblastoma development. Machine learning methods were used to identify the most informative THz and IR spectral ranges associated with glioma molecular markers provided the best distinguishing animals with and without glioblastoma.

Index Terms: Attenuated Total Reflection Fourier Transform Infrared

articleTitle: Drone-mounted Optical Fiber-fed Millimeter-wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In order to expand the use of millimeter-wave (MMW) radars in non-destructive inspection applications, a drone-mounted radar system has been developed by using the photonic techniques. The radar unit mounted on the drone weights less than 500 g, and is connected to the optical signal generator placed on the ground via an optical fiber cable. The system provides fast data acquisition speed of 0.4 msec for a single sweep over 26-GHz bandwidth, which corresponds to 10-mm spatial resolution for the range detection. The developed radar system has successfully been applied to the wall of a real chimney to measure the thickness of refractory materials.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Surface Plasmon Michelson Interferometer at the Novosibirsk Terahertz Free-Electron Laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here we present experimental results of testing the surface plasmon (SP) Michelson interferometer in the terahertz range using free-electron laser radiation. The device is designed for study of thin-layer samples on a conductive substrate. The interferometer consists of flat mirrors and a transparent plate for reflection and splitting of SP beams. The interference pattern in this device is formed by SPs. The results of the experiments have shown that the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of the SPs propagating along a plane metal with a dielectric coating can be determined.

articleTitle: 280 GHz Radiation Source Driven by a 1064nm Continuous-Wave Dual-Frequency Vertical External Cavity Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the first THz emission at 280 GHz excited by a Continuous-Wave Dual-Frequency Vertical-External-Cavity Semiconductor Laser emitting at 1064 nm and using a long carrier-lifetime plasmonic-based photomixer. These encouraging results pave the way toward coherent, tunable, compact, powerful, and low-cost terahertz sources working at room temperature.

articleTitle: Augmented reality terahertz (AR-THz) interface for imaging and sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In order to be able to use a handled portable terahertz sensor, a solution combining augmented reality and a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is proposed. The achieved architecture ensures simple handling during the acquisition process while the result visualization can be performed in live directly with a smartphone, with a 3D live superimposed augmented reality view.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Studies on Compression and Transport of an Intense Electron Beam in the Channel of sub-mm FEL
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Project of submillimeter FEL based on a relativistic electron beam is developed at BINP in collaboration with IAP. The beam with parameters E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>= 5−20 MeV, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>= 1−2 kA, τ= 160−200 ns is produced at the exit of an induction linac. According to theoretical prediction, this beam allows us to produce pulses of coherent submm-radiation (0.3-1 THz) with record power of a sub-GW level and energy content up to ~ 100 J. The paper presents the results of simulations and the experiments on the beam compression and transport in a vacuum channel of sub-mm FEL.

articleTitle: Foreign Object Debris Detection Performance Improvement Evaluation of a 90 GHz Band Millimeter-Wave Radar System in Airport Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To ensure the safety and security of airport runway operations, the automatic foreign object debris (FOD) detection system has been developed recently. We have been working on a FOD detection system based on a distributed-type millimeter-wave radar sensor operating in the 90 GHz band. In this paper, the sensitivity improvement of the radar, which is mainly achieved by using signal processing, is discussed based on experimental results at the actual airport runway. The reflection power of the typical 9 FODs is measured at various angles. The detection probabilities are then calculated using the measured results. At 307 m, the detection probabilities of 7 types of the FOD, including small FOD such as a 3 cm piece of asphalt and a 2 cm length M8 bolt, are 100%. These findings support the radar sensor’s improved detection performance.

articleTitle: Heterodyne Spectroscopy with a 225 – 255 GHz SiGe BiCMOS Receiver for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Molecular spectroscopy of gases is an important method for various applications on Earth and in space. In the millimeter-wave / terahertz range, many molecules have rotational transitions and are distinguishable by their spectral fingerprint. We analyze the performance of a heterodyne receiver fabricated in SiGe BiCMOS technology, which operates at room temperature and is tunable from 225 GHz to 255 GHz. At 241 GHz, the double sideband noise temperature of the receiver is approximately 20,000 K at 1.5 GHz intermediate frequency and the Allan time is 1 s. First heterodyne measurements of methanol emission lines were successfully performed in laboratory experiments.

articleTitle: THz s-SNOM Imaging Of Logarithmic Spiral Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Probing the near-field of photonic components at sub-wavelength scale is of high interest to improve the design of future THz devices. We report on the THz near-field imaging of logarithmic spiral antennas by scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). Our results demonstrate that the s-SNOM technique allows to access the electric field distribution on the arms of an antenna and reveals non-trivial features at the center of the component.

articleTitle: On the Modelling of the Quasi-Optical Coupling between Two Photoconductive Antennas under Pulsed Laser Illumination
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photoconductive antennas (PCA) are promising candidates for high-resolution imaging applications. They have been investigated in transmission when the receiver is a power detector. Here we consider another PCA as the receiver and develop a model of the quasi-optical (QO) coupling between the transmitter and receiver under pulsed laser illumination. Specifically, a field matching technique is used to evaluate the open-circuit voltage of the receiver. Based on this voltage, the spectral mutual coupling between the two PCAs, including the QO path can be evaluated. A bow-tie antenna feed is used as an example to show the coupling coefficient.

articleTitle: Remote radar-camera vital sign monitoring system using a graph-based extraction algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Mm-wave radar and video-based technologies have shown potentials for contactless detection of vital signs. However, state-of-the-art signal processing based vital sign extraction methods are prone to disruptions, such as motion corruption. In this work, we propose a novel graph-based segmentation algorithm for improved accuracy and robustness. We also developed a combined radar-camera system to integrate with the proposed algorithm. The test results on both mmWave radar and camera systems were found to be of high correlations (0.95-0.97) with the golden standard. Our system provides a viable and robust approach for the increasingly popular remote cardiovascular sensing and diagnosing posed by Covid-19.

articleTitle: Laser Terahertz Emission Microscopy of Gold Nanorods forming a Coffee-stain Ring on a Semiconductor Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study the influence of resonant gold nanorod deposited on an InAs surface to enhance the terahertz (THz) emission induced by the photo-Dember effect. With the nanorods forming a coffee-stain ring, we observe a variation in the induced THz field, which we image with Laser THz Emission Microscopy (LTEM). Here, we observe an enhancement of up to 30% of the THz signal measured from a bare InAs surface. On the other hand, clustering of nanorods in the central region leads to a suppression of THz signal where less than 80% of the signal measured from the bare surface is obtained. By preparing several samples with the same method but varying the number of nanorods, we are able to study the correlation between the nanorod concentration and the THz signal enhancement.

articleTitle: Mass-production of terahertz devices
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We fabricated a terahertz (THz) polarizer and a bandpass filter using an industrial roll-to-roll press to print silver nanoparticle ink onto polyethylene terephthalate (PET). The functionality of these devices has been studied with THz time domain spectroscopy. By adding a second layer, the performance of the printed devices has been improved. We have shown that this fabrication method can be used for the mass-production of THz devices at affordable price.

articleTitle: A terahertz synthetic aperture radar with centimeter-level resolution
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Compared with microwave synthetic aperture radar (SAR), terahertz (THz) SAR has advantages of higher frequency, higher resolution, higher frame rate and so on. Meanwhile, THz SAR is able to penetrate through cloud, smoke and dust with low attenuation, which leads to the applications of high-resolution imaging and target recognition in complex battlefield environment. In this paper, the results of carborne 5-GHz THz SAR imaging test are demonstrated. Besides, we have verified the design of broadband THz SAR imaging system and the key technique of high-frequency vibration compensation. The resolution of THz SAR is about 5 cm×5 cm, which provides a foundation for the research of high resolution THz SAR imaging.

articleTitle: Study on 340GHz H-plane Feed-in Staggered Double Vane Slow Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a novel H-plane coupling structure is proposed to reduce the conductive loss and processing difficulty of the device, which is applied to 340GHz staggered double vane slow wave structure for simulation and experiment. The final cold-test results show that the transmission coefficient is around -8dB in the range from 325GHz to 345GHz, and the corresponding reflection coefficient is below -10dB.

articleTitle: Photonic Generation of Barker-code Phase-Coded Terahertz Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A scheme for generating Barker-code phase-coded terahertz signals is proposed and experimentally demonstrated based on optical frequency combs (OFC) and optical heterodyne. A dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator (DPMZM) is employed for modulation implementation, where a radio frequency is applied to one arm, and the Barker-code is used to drive the other. In the experiment, we successfully generate a 10 Gbit/s Barkercode phase-coded THz signal at 357 GHz with a π phase shift, which can be potentially used in the THz pulse compression radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz Beam Steering based on CMOS Tunable Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS-based tunable device to realize electromagnetic (EM) beam steering in the THz frequency domain. The device consists of 8×8 array with double layer dumbbell-liked metamaterial (DL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>M) unit. The phase response of the THz wave can be manipulated through two MOS switches connected to the metamaterial unit. The design is implemented in the 180nm process and can achieve a maximum beam steering angle of 35° at 1.26 THz according to the simulation results. The highly integrated device demonstrates the potential of the active CMOS metamaterials for THz adaptive beamforming.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Metamaterial Absorber with Low Infrared Emissivity
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work a broadband optically transparent flexible metamaterial wave absorber with low infrared emissivity is proposed. A broadband microwave absorption rate of greater than 90% from 4.44 to 20.65 GHz with a low infrared emissivity of 0.36 was obtained. Due to the use of optically transparent, lightweight and flexible polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) as substrates, it is very popular in practical engineering applications and has practical applications of multifunctional stealth technology.

articleTitle: Studies on a Microfabricated Traveling-Wave Tube With Planar Microstrip Slow-Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Planar microstrip slow-wave structures (SWS) for a miniaturized low-voltage traveling-wave tube (TWT) in V-, W-, and D-band are designed, fabricated and tested. The low-cost and flexible technology for fabrication of such structures based on magnetron sputtering and laser ablation is developed. The wideband input/output couplers providing low reflection loss are designed and simulated. 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) modeling of beam-wave interaction in the V-band planar TWT predicts over 20 W saturated power.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Power of Deep Unfolding Networks to TomoSAR 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Deep unfolding networks have been proved to be able to achieve super-resolution (SR). Different from sparsity regularization methods, deep unfolding networks can speed up the imaging process and own good robustness against noise. However, the optimal network design and maximum SR ability of deep unfolding networks have not been quantified. In this paper, the optimal number of layers and the SR extremity of the network are confirmed by simulation. And some sparsity regularization methods are compared with the proposed method. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of SR imaging and accuracy.

articleTitle: Terahertz RTD Chip Backside-coupled to Photonic-crystal Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The incorporation of active components to micro scale photonic devices is beneficial to building fully integrated systems in the terahertz region. In this work we introduce a center-fed slot-antenna resonant tunneling diode (RTD) chip that is backside-coupled to a photonic crystal waveguide. Experiments revealed stable oscillation at 346 GHz and efficient coupling.

articleTitle: Development and experimental tests of 250W/526 GHz/CW second harmonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the gyrotron operating at the second harmonic of the gyrofrequency at a frequency of 526 GHz, radiation power of 250 W was obtained in the continuous wave generation mode. The indicated value is several times higher than all known world analogs. Experimental results open new perspectives of gyrotron application for spectroscopy, where both high frequency and high-power are needed.

articleTitle: Study of absorption and scattering of terahertz wave in inhomogeneous dusty plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The dusty plasma sheath formed during the reentry process of hypersonic vehicle will block the propagation of electromagnetic wave, causing problem in detection. Terahertz detection is a potential solution to this problem. When terahertz wave propagate through the dusty plasma sheath, both resonance absorption and scattering would lead to attenuation of terahertz wave. In this work, the propagation characteristics of terahertz wave in dusty plasma have been studied combining scattering matrix method and Mie scattering theory. The results will help to find the optimum detection frequency for reentry vehicle.

articleTitle: Real-Time Distance Measurement using a Subcarrier FMCW Radar based on a Terahertz-wave Resonant-Tunneling-Diode Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on real-time distance measurement in the terahertz range using a resonant-tunneling-diode (RTD) oscillator by applying the frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar principle to a subcarrier of the terahertz wave. Compared with our previous report, the measurement time was reduced from above one minute to below 5 ms, an improvement of over four orders of magnitude. We illustrate the improvement through an experiment in which we measure the distance to a moving target.

articleTitle: Configuration of a MEMS-based Terahertz Reflectarray Using a Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate the configuration of a MEMS-based terahertz reflectarray using a genetic algorithm for continuous beam steering with the capability of manipulating the beam pattern. Two different optimization goals are considered: maximizing the directivity and minimizing the sidelobe level. As preliminary results, we show calculated and simulated radiation patterns where the beam is successfully steered to 45° at 0.3 THz without grating lobes. For the first optimization goal, we achieve a directivity of 16.7 dBi at the desired angle, whereas we suppress the sidelobe level from -13.7 dB to -16 dB for the second optimization goal.

articleTitle: Compact single layer Dual-Band Dual Polarized Transmissive Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter with High Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dual band Linear to circular polarization converters are widely used in modern communication systems. Requirements of wide operational bandwidth, simple and ultra-thin design, and stable performances for oblique incidence angles make design of such converters quite challenging. In this paper, a single-side layered metasurface is presented which performs in dual wide-bands and converts incident x(y) polarized wave into transmitted LHCP(RHCP) wave from 11.05~16.75GHz (41%) and RHCP(LHCP) from 34.16~43.03GHz (23%) which qualifies for numerous practical applications including millimeter-wave-communication.

articleTitle: A Comparison between THz Spectroscopy and GC-MS by Detection of Isopropanol in Human Breath
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a comparison between THz spectroscopy and gas chromatography-mass spectroscopy (GC-MS), which is considered the gold-standard for sensitive breath detection. For this purpose, we analyzed human breath samples with both methods and discuss key figures as well as advantages and disadvantages for this application. As an example, the detection of isopropanol is presented which was exhaled after hand disinfection of a volunteer. THz spectroscopy provides results consistent with GC-MS and even distinguishes conformers of isopropanol. The sensitivity of the THz spectrometer for isopropanol is roughly 500 times smaller in this case, but can be improved depending on the species and measurement parameters.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimization Method Based on Fuzzy Control Theory for Design of High Compression Ratio Sheet Beam Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel optimization method is proposed for design of high compression ratio sheet beam electron gun. Since the traditional electron gun design requires more manual debugging, this optimization method combining fuzzy control theory and genetic algorithm greatly reduces the time cost to obtain the global optimal solution. With this method, a W-band sheet beam electron gun with beam compression ratio of 10:1 is optimized and about 70% of the time is saved compared to manual optimization.

articleTitle: Phase Locking of 3.5-THz and 4.7-THz Quantum-Cascade Lasers Using a Schottky Diode Harmonic Mixer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: High frequency accuracy and stability are important requirements for local oscillators in terahertz heterodyne spectrometers. We report on a phase-locked loop for quantum-cascade lasers (QCLs) operating at 3.5 and 4.7 THz, two very important frequencies in atmospheric science and astronomy. The QCLs are locked to the multiplied output of a frequency synthesizer using a Schottky diode harmonic mixer.

articleTitle: Video-rate Suspicious Object Detection for MMW Walk-through Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Near-range millimeter wave imaging techniques for persons have been widely used in public security field. To improve the throughput and security as well, a suspicious object detection method is designed for the Walk Through System we built. Simple Online and Realtime Tracking algorithm is applied based on the detection result of YOLOv5 in in each frame. The method can effectively detect objects at a video rate of 10Hz.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Detection of Tobacco Filter Capsule by Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Method of none-destructive detection of tobacco filter capsule by Terahertz Time domain spectroscopy is proposed. Flavor capsule in the cigarettes filter contains liquid spices, which could help improving cigarette taste. The absence, location, and damage condition of filter capsule would affect the tobacco quality tobacco factory’s economic benefit and credibility. Inline quality inspection of tobacco filter requires accurately locate the flavor capsules in the filter. The filter capsule perfectly matches THz spatial resolution. In experiment, transmission Terahertz time domain spectroscopy imaging system was employed to measure the tobacco filer capsule. The result show that two-capsules in the tobacco filter can be positioned and distinguished by THz transmittance imaging. The result shows that Terahertz technology is a promising application for tobacco filter capsule quality control and production efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network based denoising method for rapid THz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose our own convolutional neural network (CNN) structure as a post-processing method for the rapid THz Imaging in Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy(THz-TDS). The experiment results show that our approach can greatly reduce the noise and artifacts in the collected under-sampled THz images, which in turn benefits the rapid THz imaging technique by allowing higher acquisition rates. In our setup, 5 times higher acquisition rates can be realized. Moreover, this approach needs no extra hardware cost, and since the training has been done offline, the processing time in practice can be ignored. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time applying deep learning(DL) methods into rapid THz imaging technique, which would inspire researchers to explore more DL based applications and technologies for THz technique development.

articleTitle: 3D Rectification Effect on Plasmonic THz Detection by InP-Based Dual-Grating-Gate High-Electron-Mobility Transistor
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that the photovoltaic responsivity in an InP-based dual-grating-gate HEMT plasmonic THz detector with the gate-readout configuration is significantly enhanced by a positive gate bias application due to the nonlinear rectification effect at the InGaAs/InAlAs heterobarrier.

articleTitle: All-Electronic Terahertz 3-D Imaging System Based on FMCW
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents an all-electronic Terahertz (THz) 3-D sub-millimeter imaging system based on frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW), whose frequency ranges from 340GHz to 500GHz. For high-resolution cross-range imaging, the focused method is used instead of the traditional synthetic aperture technique. The imaging performance of the system is verified by some experimental results.

articleTitle: Characterization of graphene Drude conductivity by terahertz and infrared spectroscopy methods
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Extreme sensitivity of graphene films to a technological transfer and the device fabrication steps requires the development of non-destructive contactless characterization methods. Here we have employed the methods of terahertz time-domain spectroscopy and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy to investigate the graphene electrical conductivity, described in terms of the high-frequency Drude model. Commercial CVD graphene samples were wet-transferred to different substrates in order to demonstrate advantages of remote characterization methods over contact-based approaches for determination of carrier density and mobility values in two-dimensional materials.

articleTitle: Frequency Stabilization of Megawatt-Class 140 GHz Gyrotrons at W7-X Using an Off-the-Shelf PLL System
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An off-the-shelf Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) system is used to stabilize the free-running oscillation frequencies of the 140 GHz, 1 MW CW gyrotrons of the companies Thales, France, and CPI, USA, that both operate at the ECRH system of the Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) stellarator at IPP Greifswald, Germany. Both tubes are equipped with diode-type Magnetron Injection Guns (MIGs). Considering each of both type of gyrotrons as a Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO), each individual gyrotron is controlled by the variation of the body voltage. The results of the experiments demonstrate the capability of the developed and implemented inexpensive off-the-shelf PLL system. It is possible to stabilize the oscillation frequency within a full -20 dB bandwidth of < 100 kHz. Applications such as Collective Thomson Scattering (CTS) systems to accurately diagnose the ions in fusion plasmas could benefit from this development in future.

articleTitle: High Aperture Efficiency Plastic Lens Antenna for Scanning Lens Phased Array at 180 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we present a plastic resonant leaky-wave lens antenna with high aperture efficiency (>80%) over a 1:2 bandwidth centered at 180 GHz. This antenna can be integrated in a scanning lens phased array architecture for next-generation wireless and sensing applications that require high-directivity steerable beams. The high aperture efficiency is achieved thanks to the combination of annular corrugations in the ground plane with a leaky-wave resonant cavity. A WR-5 (140-220 GHz) prototype is manufactured and measured in terms of reflection coefficient, radiation patterns, directivity, losses, cross-polarization and scan performance, showing excellent agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Beam-Plasma Interaction System Providing Ten Megawatt Power of THz Radiation Flux in Microsecond Pulse
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Submillimeter wave generation due to the intense interaction of a relativistic electron beam (REB) with magnetized plasma is studied at GOL-PET facility. In a plasma column with density ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> the e-beam (0.5 MeV/15kA/6μs) generates a well-directed 1 mm wavelength flux of ~ 10 MW power. Paper presents measurement results of the radiation spectral composition in 0.1 – 0.6 THz band and the energy distribution function of the beam electrons at various plasma density distributions. The obtained results are discussed in the consideration of theoretical models.

articleTitle: Biomedical Applications of Terahertz Near-field Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the THz near-field nano-imaging of Bacillus cereus and Corona Virus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) spike fake virus utilizing THz scattering near-field optical microscopy (SNOM). Here, it shows that bacteria and virus can be distinguished from other substances by THz near-field imaging. And we can use the THz time-domain spectrometer (TDS) scattering near field microscope(s-SNOM) to obtain the spectrum of different substances (bacteria and their substrate), then analyzing the differences between them from their specific responses in THz. This is of great significance to development of the terahertz near-field biology.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-loss Terahertz Transition from GCPW to Rectangular Waveguide with Filter Performance Using Multiple Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel low-loss transition from grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) to rectangular waveguide (RWG) is proposed in the paper. Multiple resonators are introduced to realize the wideband transition structure with good performance of out-of-band rejection. The main structure is designed under the bottom grounded plane of the GCPW transmission line in order to reduce radiation losses and improve the transmission efficiency, and moreover the transition has the advantage of simple fabrication and micro-assembly processes. A 0.2 THz filtering transition is designed as an example.

articleTitle: Design of a Ka Band Broadband 90° Phase Shifter Base on GGW
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A low phase error broadband phase shifter based on the groove gap waveguide (GGW) is presented. In the proposed structure, unlike the way of quarter wavelength sections to obtain the phase shift, the phase shift can be obtained by stretching the broad side of the GGW and placing a stepped-ridge at the bottom layer, which are more suitable in development of symmetry and compact beam-forming networks of antennas. From fabrication point of view, the phase shifter based on the GGW is that it is removing the need for electrical contact between the different metal layers which considerably simplifies the manufacturing and assembly processes. The proposed phase shifter is designed to achieve 90° phase shift with the phase error less than 1.4° for a frequency range of 27-38 GHz compared to the equal length reference waveguide.

articleTitle: Line of sight THz detector using TeraFET spectrometers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The line of sight detector using TeraFETs operating as THz spectrometers is simulated with the validated THz SPICE unified charge control model for Si MOSFETs. The model uses the nonlinear transmission line of the segmented channel resistances, capacitances and Drude inductances. The THz spectrometers oriented in different directions give different response maps with respect to the angles of the incident THz radiation. Combining these response maps allows for the determination of the THz radiation angles and therefore the line of sight detection.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of A Directional Dual-Beam Antenna-Coupled High-Temperature Superconducting Balanced Terahertz Receiver
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work presents the design and simulation of a quasi-optically coupled high-temperature superconducting (HTS) balanced terahertz receiver. The design features an integrated lens antenna excited by two concentric-slots-shaped thin-film radiators, which radiates highly directional dual-beams for coupling the radio-frequency (RF) and local-oscillator (LO) signals, respectively. Besides, a 340-GHz balanced HTS Josephson-junction heterodyne receiver circuit is carefully designed in terms of matching, isolation and wideband transmission. Detailed numerical modelling and simulations are conducted for verifying the concept of design and the performance of the balanced antenna-coupled HTS receiver.

articleTitle: Broad-Band Miniaturized Antenna Implementation Working Among 57-70 GHz V-Band for 5th Generation and Beyond Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An Ultra-wideband antenna for 5G V-band applications was proposed in this work. A conventional circular patch antenna was modified by using two set of fractal patches to increase the operational bandwidth of the antenna. While a circular slot was utilized to adjust the radiation pattern of the proposed work. The antenna offers an ultrawideband of < 30% with reference to the central frequency of 65 GHz. Moreover, the broadside radiation pattern, high gain and efficiency will make the proposed work a strong candidate for wideband applications using V-band spectrum.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Transmission Line with Harmonic sub-THz Power Generation in a 40 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This contribution presents a broadband 10 GHz to 0.15 THz power generation with a nonlinear transmission line technique in a 40 nm CMOS technology. In this work, 110 elementary sections of varactors are embedded in the nonlinear transmission line, and it is fully compatible with CMOS technology for a sub-THz harmonic generation. With this compact solution, the area of this sub-THz power generation is 588 × 660 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. With a 6 dBm 10 GHz input signal, the output power could cover from 20 GHz to 150 GHz. At 100 GHz, the power is -37 dBm, while it is -40 dBm at -150 GHz.

articleTitle: Learning-Based THz Multi-Layer Imaging for High-Capacity Positioning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper considers terahertz (THz) multi-layer imaging for three-dimensional (3D) positioning and encoders. A learning-based approach is introduced to address challenges such as 1) depth variation, 2) shadowing effect, and 3) content recognition at the back surface of each layer. Experimental validation on a three-layer sample with contents on both front and back surfaces confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Terahertz Biomedical Application Research
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We reviewed the recent progress in applications of Terahertz waves in biomedical research, summarized the relevant methods with their advantages and disadvantages. In addition, we proposed a three-step one-way terahertz model, providing detailed flow analysis for terahertz technology in the biomedical detection: 1) Biomarker determination; 2) Mixture interference removal; and 3) Individual difference removal. These results have profound implications for the rapid, accurate and early detection of diseases.

articleTitle: Investigation of THz transmission through semi-insulating substrate with a thin conductive layer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Simple analytical model for description of THz time-domain spectroscopy data was found investigating high-frequency characteristics of semi-insulating substrate with thin conductive layer. Developed method was validated on commercial AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor structures and supported by dc Hall measurements of two-dimensional electron gas density and mobility at temperature range of 80-300 K.

articleTitle: Compact and Inexpensive Terahertz System Driven by Monolithically Integrated Commercial Light Sources
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the dissemination of new methods and applications in terahertz spectroscopy and terahertz nondestructive testing, the need for compact and low-cost systems is increasing to enable small companies and research groups to work in these fields. Therefore, we present a compact and inexpensive terahertz spectrometer, achieving dimensions of 300 mm x 270 mm x 110 mm, a bandwidth of 1.22 THz, and a peak dynamic range of 70 dB.

articleTitle: Traveling wave TeraFET spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the results of the traveling wave spectrometer simulation using the unified charge control TeraFET SPICE model. The model is in good agreement with the 32nm Si MOSFET model in TCAD. The simulations show that the detected response could be dramatically increased by feeding the phase-shifted terahertz (THz) signal into the gate and source terminals of TeraFET amplifiers with the first stage dominating the enhancement. The traveling wave TeraFET spectrometer approach enables orders of magnitude improvement in the response compared to the basic TeraFET spectrometer without drain-to-source current. When properly calibrated, it also allows for a more accurate determination of the cross-over frequency and facilitates the implementation of the frequency to digital converter.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of a Slow-wave Structure for the V-band Backward-Wave Oscillator with a Pseudospark-Source Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The results of fabrication and cold-test study of the slow-wave interaction structure for the V-band backward-wave oscillator with a pseudospark-sourced sheet electron beam are presented. The proposed interaction structure is comprised of a truncated sine waveguide with wideband-matched output couplers. The slow-wave structure is designed, simulated, and fabricated by CNC-micro milling. The results of characterization of the microfabricated SWS sample by the scanning electron microscopy and stylus profilometry technique are presented. Preliminary results of experimental studies of electromagnetic parameters and their comparison with the numerical simulation are presented. The electron gun providing a high-current-density pseudospark sheet electron beam is also developed.

articleTitle: THz ISCI: Terahertz Integrated Sensing, Communication and Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The Terahertz (0.1-10 THz) band provides huge potential for supporting unprecedented data rates and millimeter-level accurate sensing. Terahertz integrated sensing, communication and intelligence (ISCI) is viewed as one of the key technologies to realize connected intelligence in next-generation systems. In this paper, integrated waveform, dynamic beamforming, signal detection and artificial intelligence techniques are investigated for THz ISCI.

articleTitle: Fast Three-dimensional Terahertz Imaging with Continuous-wave Photomixing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A high-speed frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system is proposed for three-dimensional (3D) terahertz imaging. In order to obtain a high range resolution of mm-order together with fast data acquisition speed, the photonics-based approach is adopted. Thanks to the high-speed frequency sweep of a tunable laser device, the wide bandwidth ranged from 200 GHz to 420 GHz, which corresponds to a range resolution of ~1.3 mm, can be achieved within 35 msec. Furthermore, the 3D imaging of a multi-layer model was demonstrated with quasioptical imaging system, both range and spatial resolution can achieve to ~1.3 mm without using complicated signal processing.

articleTitle: Calibration-Free Gas Quantification through Wavelength Modulation Spectroscopy in the Millimeter-Wave/Terahertz Range
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter-Wave/Terahertz (mmW/THz) spectroscopy affords high precision and specificity, useful for analyzing complex gas mixtures. In conjunction with wavelength modulation spectroscopy (WMS), it stands out as a sensitive technique for trace gas detection. The complex nature of the WMS absorption line shape, however, remains challenging to quantify and interpret. In this work, we propose a practical procedure for processing and analyzing the WMS signal to derive a calibrationfree quantification of the target gas. To validate the method, we compared the results to reference measurements of methanol and water and found a good agreement.

articleTitle: Imaging with an Ultra-High Repetition Rate Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy System Driven by a Mode-Locked Laser Diode
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Mode-locked laser diodes (MLLDs) are attractive as light sources for compact terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) systems for imaging applications. A great advantage of their ultra-high repetition rate is that objects can be imaged at arbitrary distances independent of the length of the optical delay unit (ODU) of the spectrometer. The downside of the ultra-high repetition rate is that it generates only a small unambiguous imaging window. In this work, we show first images acquired with a THz-TDS system driven by a MLLD.

articleTitle: An estimation of high-power sub-THz gyrotron based system for space debris detection and Moon scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The free space radar equation has been analyzed for the field of parameters of a mighty source of sub-terahertz electromagnetic waves used for radar applications and long-range space telecommunication in surface and ground-to-space channels. Some new potential tasks of such coherent radars have been found feasible including active search for space debris and new radar astronomy tasks.

articleTitle: Development of "Flying" RF-Undulators with Regular and Profiled Parameters for FELs of Compton-Type
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Conception of Compton FEL-scattrons is under development at IAP RAS and aimed at reducing energy of a driving relativistic electron beam, increasing efficiency of the electron-wave interaction and achieving relative compactness of the generator. The basis of this concept is RF-undulator of a new type - the so-called "flying" undulator, which represent short microwave pulse that synchronously propagates with driving electron bunch and provides pumping of its oscillations. Profiling parameters of "flying" undulator allows realization of the non-resonant trapping regime resulting in further enhancement of the FEL efficiency. Present paper is devoted to the design parameters, results of simulations and "cold" tests of regular and profiled "flying" undulators realized in the Ka and W bands.

articleTitle: Analysis of debonding defects of GFRP in terahertz nondestructive testing based on FDTD
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The measured optical parameters of glass fiber reinforced composites in 0.1-1.5 THz waveband are optimized by Debye model with terahertz pulse as the input light source. Based on the finite-difference time-domain method, the propagation characteristics of terahertz wave in GFRP bonding defect model are numerically simulated, and the time-domain simulation waveforms and B-scan diagrams of non debonding defect, 50um debonding defect and 100um debonding defect are analyzed, and the variation characteristics with the thickness of debonding defect are given. It provides theoretical support for terahertz nondestructive testing and evaluation of GFRP.

articleTitle: Design of a Half-Maxwell-Fisheye Lens Based on the Surface Plasmon Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spoof surface plasmons (SSPs) can manipulate electromagnetic waves with subwavelength prints, which offers possibilities for many applications. To generate the SSPs propagating on a two-dimensional (2D) scale, the all-dielectric or dielectric-metal metasurfaces are generally exploited. However, the power capacity of the all-dielectric or dielectric-metal metasurfaces is relatively low. In this work, a 2D groove metal array is utilized to generate the SSPs. The dimension of the grooves is changed to possess the SSPs propagating on it. Based on this principle, a 2D half-Maxwell-fisheye lens is proposed utilizing the groove metal array, on which a spot on one side of the lens can diverge to a plane wave on the exit facet in the simulation. The all-metal half-Maxwell-fisheye lens is capable to be employed for high-power application scenarios.

articleTitle: Resonance Fabry-Perot Interferometer for Ultra-high Resolution Spectroscopy of Free Electron Laser Radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Pulse-periodical free electron lasers with an optical cavity can have a fine and always have a hyperfine spectral structure of radiation due to the coherence of output pulses, which are parts of different or the same intra-cavity light pulse, respectively. The optimal instrument for measuring these structures is the resonance Fabry-Perot interferometer described in this article. The composition of transverse supermodes of the NovoFEL in various regimes was revealed by the device, operating in a frequency-domain mode with a 5•10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> resolution. The time-domain regime of the interferometer, which has practically no limitations, made it possible to accurately measure the monochromaticity of the NovoFEL modes, which turned out to be equal to 2.2•10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>.

articleTitle: Ultrafast dynamics of optical phonons in α-quartz launched by THz wave and femtosecond laser combined excitation source
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We use the terahertz (THz) wave generated from the 1550 nm femtosecond laser excited DAST crystal and an 800 nm femtosecond laser to jointly focus on the α-quartz crystal, and prompt it to produce ultrafast coherent phonon dynamic effect. The experimental phenomena were detected by means of THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy. We found that when the two excitation beams have different relative time delays, the oscillation frequencies of the phonon generated by the quartz crystal shift. It is of great importance for us to study phonon dynamics of quartz crystal and other materials.

articleTitle: Characterization of non-idealities in optical Nyquist pulses for THz signal sampling metrology
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Optical sinc-shaped Nyquist pulses can be utilized for high-speed communication with minimal error as it enables orthogonality and rectangular shape in the frequency domain, etc. Nevertheless, for metrological evaluations, the performance of the system is hampered by the presence of non-idealities. In this work, we simulate and examine the impact of two prime non-idealities: the sideband suppression ratio (SSR) and the roll-off factor of sinc-shaped reconfigurable Nyquist pulse sequences based on 3-line optical phase-locked combs at a frequency spacing of 200 GHz. Furthermore, we estimate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) error for the respective non-idealities.

articleTitle: Experiments on gyrotron frequency stabilization by resonant reflections
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper presents the experimental investigation of the gyrotron frequency stabilization by the partial reflection of its' radiation from the resonant load. The experiments were conducted using the continuous wave 28 GHz gyrotron and a quasi-optical resonator as a tunable reflector. Obtained results agree with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Landau-level radiation in current-injected monolayer graphene
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Monolayer graphene has a gapless and linear dispersion. Thanks to this unique dispersion, monolayer graphene has unequally Landau levels (LLs) and an extra LL at the charge neutral point. In this paper, we investigated the spectrum of infrared radiation from current-injected graphene under high magnetic fields. The experimental results indicate that infrared radiation is attributed to the inter-LL radiative transition with a narrower linewidth than expected from magnetotransport measurements.

articleTitle: Stimulated emission of plasmon-LO mode in narrow gap HgTe/CdHgTe quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The possibility of amplification of the coupled plasmon – optical phonon (LO) mode in an HgTe quantum wells (QWs) is theoretically considered. In a 6 nm wide QW with CdTe barriers and in a 5 nm wide QW with Cd0.7Hg0.3Te barriers grown on the (013) plane, stimulated emission of the plasmon – LO mode is possible in the frequency range corresponding to the Reststrahlen band of GaAs.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Complex Amplitude Modulation via A HEMT-Switched 1-Bit Coding Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An electrically controlled terahertz 1-bit complex amplitude modulation via an OOK (on-off-keying) resonant shifting on a coplanar meta-HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) array is proposed here. The effects of the dispersion characteristics of different two-dimensional electron gas concentrations on both phase shift and amplitude characteristics are studied. Under a low switch ratio, a broadband 180 ° reflection phase shift and an averaged -7.5 dB amplitude are attained in 0.306 ~ 0.321 THz. Considering the state of art, the proposed hybrid microstructure is capable of reprogrammable complex amplitude modulation, which has shed a light on ultrafast terahertz wavefront regulation.

articleTitle: PT-symmetry conditions for hybrid modes in a waveguide coupler
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A multimode analytical approach is used to investigate the PT-symmetry in hybrid modes of a loss-gain waveguide coupler operated in the THz range. It is shown that loss compensation in this coupler can be achieved by varying the distance between loss and gain waveguides for an arbitrary operating frequency. PT-symmetry thresholds are found for the loss-gain waveguide couplers operated in hybrid HE or EH modes with different azimuthal indices. It is shown that below these thresholds the hybrid modes are coupled. Field distribution for coupled hybrid modes is presented.

articleTitle: Water: a major requisite for the protein fibrillation as revealed by THz spectroscopy measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We explore the change in the collective hydration of water during the protein fibrillation (native →intermediate →fibril) of a model protein bovine serum albumin using terahertz spectroscopy. We also establish that the structural makeover of the protein during the conformational transition is followed by the associated hydration.

articleTitle: Rubber Inner Cord Absence Detection using Terahertz Video Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cord reinforcement framework can effectively improve the rubber performance. The absence of cord may lead to potential safety hazard. In this paper, we successfully demonstrate the detection of cord reinforcement framework absence in rubber through comparison analysis the terahertz (THz) images with and without rubber inner cord. This work provides a solution for the rapid nondestructive detection of the missing of rubber inner cord reinforcement framework. Future work assisted by artificial intelligence enabled technology, we believe the intelligent THz imaging will provide better solution for rapid and nondestructive detection of rubber internal defects and other disruptive applications.

articleTitle: Ultrafast All-Optical Terahertz Modulation with Sulfur-Passivated GaAs
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With a surface-passivated GaAs, a performance-enhanced, ultrafast, all-optical spatial terahertz modulator was realized. The lower surface recombination rate and longer carrier lifetime induced by passivation render passivated-GaAs superior to pure-GaAs in modulation depth (MD) at a little sacrifice of response rate, eliminating its dependence on intensive laser. At low photodoping levels, the maximum of 1.6-times enhancement in MD was achieved. When the power increased to 60 mW, comparable MD of 94% to that in Si-based one at equivalent photodoping, and simultaneously ultrafast response of 69 MHz which is much faster than 100-kHz level by Si-based, was obtained. This performance-enhanced, ultrafast modulator is highly desired in actual situations and offers a viable avenue to breaking the compromise between MD and speed.

articleTitle: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of Microcystin-LR using THz-Aptamer Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A combination of Terahertz (THz) emission and aptamer technologies has a crucial impact on the highly sensitive and rapid detection of small toxic molecules such as microcystin-LR (MC-LR). THz chemical microscope (TCM) is a unique THz aptasensor that has been successfully used for monitoring MC-LR molecules in buffer and complex samples. Our results show that our TCM aptasensor has an excellent detection limit of 50 ng/L as well as the assay time is about 15 min. Compared with other biosensors such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), our TCM aptasensor provides a rapid and sensitive assay.

articleTitle: Terahertz Near-field Inspection of Metallic Nano-gap Grating for Contrast-Enhanced Interaction with Two-dimensional Materials
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Near-field inspection of metallic nano-gap gratings can be used to efficiently monitor terahertz (THz) interaction with two-dimensional (2D) materials. Localized field enhancement at the nano-gap region leads to higher absorption of the transmitted THz field and thus to a higher contrast of otherwise barely visible 2D materials. In this study, a significant enhancement of THz contrast was observed with high-resolution THz near-field imaging at graphene and MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The resulting effective conductance and THz absorption have been quantified on a sub-wavelength scale using a photoconductive near-field microprobebased THz-time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) system.

articleTitle: Research Progresses of Millimeter and Terahertz Waves Traveling Wave Tube in AIRCAS
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The Terahertz (THz) traveling wave tube (TWT) is developed for demands of broad applications, such as broad bandwidth communications, biomedicine, security check, basic subject research, etc. Through solved and grasped key technologies of THz TWT, some THz TWTs has been designed, fabricated and measured at frequency W-band, G-band and J-band. In this paper, the research progresses of THz TWT in Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS) will be described.

articleTitle: Switchable Terahertz Meta-lens Based on Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a composite dynamic metasurface embedded with vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is designed. The working state of the metal-vanadium composite metasurface can be changed by temperature-excited insulation-metal transition of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. According to this property, we designed a meta-lens with a switch function. In the insulating state, the phase coverage can reach 2π at 0.34 THz, and the amplitude can keep a high level so that the focusing function can be realized. However, in the metallic state, the reflected waves of the elements with different parameters are almost in the same phase and maintain a high amplitude, showing as plane waves. It is believed that the meta-lens designed by us will enrich the family of THz metasurfaces.

articleTitle: THz ratchet effect in HgTe-based lateral superlattices
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the observation of terahertz radiation induced ratchet effects in HgTe/HgCdTe-based quantum well (QWs) structures with a comb-like dual-grating-gate (DGG) structures. For investigations, we used various HgTe QWs with thickness of the 8.0, 7.0, and 6.3 nm, corresponding to parabolic dispersion with inverted band structure (8.0 and 7.0 nm) and linear dispersion (6.3 nm).

articleTitle: Output Cavity of Gyroklystron Operated in Dual-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gyroklystron operated in dual-band has profound research significance as a high-power microwave source, which can reduce the size, weight, and cost and contribute to the research of dual-band radar systems. In this paper, the theoretical analysis and simulation are used to design the output cavity operated in dual-band, the resonant frequency and quality factor of which are 9.34 GHz and 122 in X-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</inf> mode, 16.8 GHz and 475 in Ku-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</inf> mode respectively. It lays a foundation for the beam-wave interaction of the dual-band gyroklystron. Keywords: dual-band, output cavity, Gyroklystron

articleTitle: Study Of The Possibility Of Reducing The Velocity Spread In The Electron Flow Formed By An Electron-Optical System With A Multi-Tip Field Emitter
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The possibility of decreasing the velocity spread in an electron flow formed by an electron-optical system (EOS) with a multi-tip field emitter by means of adjustable inhomogeneities of the electric field in the electron gun is demonstrated.

articleTitle: 3D reconstruction using 0.1THz Bessel CT imaging system
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Zero-order terahertz Bessel beams are diffractom-free. Therefore, unlike the traditional Gaussian beam CT, the terahertz zero-order Bessel beam used in terahertz CT imaging can improve the depth of field of the imaging system. At the same time, the imaging system has high lateral resolution. Bessel beam CT was used to scan a variety of samples at the same time and the reconstruction results were obtained. The reconstructed sections and three-dimensional structures of the scanned samples were clearly seen.

articleTitle: Terahertz Absorption Characteristics of Potassium Salt Solution Based on Microfluidic Chip
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The vibrational and rotational energy levels of many biological macromolecules are in the terahertz band. Therefore, terahertz technology plays an important role in the field of biochemistry. However, due to the strong absorption of THz wave by hydrogen bonds in water, many research groups combine terahertz spectroscopy and microfluidic technology to reduce the influence of hydrogen bonding on biomolecules. We fabricated THz microfluidic chips with COC with high THz transmittance to reduce the interaction distance between THz wave and aqueous solution. Finally, the terahertz transmission characteristics of five different potassium salt solutions were studied by using the chip.

articleTitle: Terahertz Quantum Cascade Laser Based on Non-uniform Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the realization of terahertz quantum cascade laser based on an antenna array, in which each unit contains two dipole antennas with slightly different widths. The device operates in single mode around 3.2THz, and the radiation efficiency can be flexibly manipulated by the width difference between the dual-antenna in each unit. Single mode emission with 30dB side-mode suppression ratio, 120 mW pulsed output power and 1% wall-plug efficiency has been demonstrated at a heat-sink temperature of 20K.

articleTitle: Photo-carrier dynamics in UV-visible pumped GaAs studied by time-resolved THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a UV-visible pump/THz-probe study to determine the photo-carrier lifetime in GaAs. Three samples (<100>, <110> and <111> oriented) were pumped from 1.56 eV to 4.15 eV. For the three orientations we observed a strong unexpected peak of the carrier lifetime around 2.6 eV.

articleTitle: Terahertz polarization detection characteristics of a photoconductive antenna detector
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system (THz-TDS) has been widely used in the fields of substance detection, composition analysis and other fields. In order to accurately obtain the optical properties of the sample, it is essential to accurately measure the polarization direction of the terahertz electric field in THz-TDS. In this paper, a dual-polarization THz time-domain spectroscopy system is reported, and a dual-polarization photoconductive antenna array detector is designed to simultaneously detect both the terahertz time domain waveform and the terahertz electric field direction. The experimental results show that the polarization contrast ratio of the detector is 556:1.

articleTitle: Electroluminescence from HgTe quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report electroluminescence experiments on HgTe/Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>Te quantum wells with inverted band structure in strong lateral electric fields. The electroluminescence is found to appear above a critical bias. Spectral measurements show emission peaks at energies around 6 meV and 70 meV corresponding to interband and intersubband transitions, respectively. The excitation mechanism is attributed to the Zener tunneling that is consistent with the current-voltage characteristics and the bias dependence of the emission intensity.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact TE□40 Mode Converter Based on Power Divider Principle
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A W-band TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">□</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</inf> mode converter with a compact structure based on three T-junction power dividers for measuring high-order overmoded mode slow-wave structures is presented. Since the T-junction discontinuity causes the port reflection, a series of matching steps were introduced in the converter. The proposed converter possessed a bandwidth of 12 GHz with the transmission coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> higher than -3 dB and port reflection S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> lower than -15 dB. More importantly, the transmission coefficient of the unwanted modes is lower than -15 dB within the bandwidth of interest.

articleTitle: Dynamic conversion between bound states in the continuum (BIC) and quasi-BIC supported by terahertz metal metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BIC) is a strong interaction of light and matter, which has attracted a wide research interest. But the dynamic conversion between quasi-BIC and BIC has not been realized for metal system. This work reports a common metal metasurface supporting symmetry-protected BIC, which consists of two rectangular strips with different lengths. We introduce the structured graphene into it and successfully achieve the dynamic conversion between quasi-BIC and BIC by reasonable parameter design and Fermi level tuning.
