abstract: Here, we have reported first that type-ii topological Dirac semimetals PtTe2, Ir<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and PdTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> enable to achieve high-speed terahertz detection technology at room temperature, combining their peculiar band structure, with topologically protected electronic states. For PtTe2, we report the first self- power capability of THz detection based on topological Dirac semimetal PtTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, displaying room-temperature photosensitivity as high as 1.6 A W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 0.12 THz with a response time less than 20 s. For Ir<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Pt doping enable tunable Fermi level, achieving the low-energy terahertz detection. For PdTe2, we further demonstrate the superb responsivity of 10 A W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 0.3 THz, fast response of 1 s and low noise-equivalent power (NEP) of 2 pW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup>, resulting from the polarization-dependent photogalvanic effect. We have also validated the application capability of the both materials by 0.3 THz imaging, showing that the devices enable THz large-area fast imaging of macroscopic samples.

articleTitle: (Cd,Mn)Te Crystals as Efficient Emitters and Detectors of Terahertz Transients
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te crystals exhibit a strong optical rectification and electro-optic effects. We present our studies on Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.55</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.45</inf>Te single crystals, operating as efficient emitters and detectors of THz radiation transients, when excited by femtosecond optical pulses.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-based Radiation Sources with Free Electrons
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: All-metal metamaterial, as a brand-new high frequency structure, can exhibit unusual electromagnetic properties in radiation sources with free electrons. In this talk, the author reports the recent progress in the reversed Cherenkov radiation, reversed Cherenkov oscillator (RCO), and metamaterial extended interaction klystron. The first experiment shows that the RCO is a really metamaterial-based device because all the dimensions are sub-wavelength. These novel radiation sources have important applications such as in the high power microwave, accelerator, medical imaging, and microwave heating.

articleTitle: Complicated Electrodynamic Systems for Sub-THz High-Harmonic Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We describe a series of works aimed at creating high-harmonic gyrotrons with cavities of complicated shapes as a way to increase efficiencies of their operation and to improve their selective properties. These works are mainly aimed at the implementation of the large-orbit gyrotrons developed at our Institute on the basis of two experimental installations. At the same time, some approaches have proved attractive also for traditional gyrotron configurations.

articleTitle: Multi-Extreme THz ESR at the Present Stage
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: As THz electron spin resonance (ESR) measurement has several advantages of high spectral resolution, ESR measurement beyond the zero-field splitting or the magnetic phase transition, it is a powerful means to study novel magnetic systems. Focusing on these advantages, we have been developing this THz ESR, and we are now extending to the multi-extreme THz ESR. Here the multi-extreme corresponds to the high magnetic field, the high pressure, the low temperature and the micro-mechanically detected highly sensitive THz ESR. Recent new developments and applications, especially focusing on the high pressure THz ESR, will be shown.

articleTitle: A Ultrabroadband Efficient Practical Terahertz Absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) Nickel (Ni) Skeleton is a kind of flexible, process easily, low-cost, broadband, and efficient terahertz absorbing material, which can achieve more than 98% absorption in the frequency range of 0.5-2.0 THz. Based on this discovery, the feasibility of making 3D skeletal metal to achieve THz absorption is proposed and experimentally verified. It is believed that this discovery can accelerate the practical application of THz absorbing materials.

articleTitle: Plasmon Enhancement of Emission and Absorption by CdSe-based Nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the resonant plasmon enhancement Raman scattering (RS), photoluminescence (PL), and IR absorption by colloidal CdSe-based nanocrystals deposited on Au nanodisk and nanoantenna arrays. Numerical simulations were applied to calculate structural parameters of nanodisks and nanoantennas for which local surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) energy coincides with interband transition energies and surface optical (SO) phonon energies in NCs, correspondingly. The enhancement factors of RS and PL depend resonantly on the nanodisk size. Tip-Enhanced Raman Scattering (TERS) imaging allowed us to carry out the local spectral analysis of CdSe NCs with nanometer spatial resolution. A design of H-type nanoantennas was chosen to achieve maximal enhanced absorption by SO phonons from 1 monolayer of NCs.

articleTitle: Terahertz Properties of Organometallic Perovskite/Graphene Oxide Composite Films
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Thin films of a composite based on CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite and graphene oxide (GO) particles were studied by the terahertz time domain spectroscopy method in the 0.2-2.9 THz spectral range. A significant increase in the terahertz absorption coefficient and the real part of the optical conductivity of the CH3NH3PbI3/GO composite was found with an increase in the content of GO particles in the composite. At the same time, it was established that the contribution of low-frequency vibrational modes in the perovskite molecule to the absorption and optical conductivity of the composite significantly decreases with an increase in the GO concentration.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on the Non-thermal Effects of CTFEL Irradiation on B16 Tumor Cells and Tissues
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Based on the CTFEL equipment, the non-thermal biological effects of strong field terahertz waves on B16 tumor cells and tissues were preliminarily studied by in-vitro and in-vivo experiments. The results of in-vitro experiments show that the death rate of B16 cells is related to the irradiation time and frequency. The results of in-vivo experiments show that strong field terahertz waves can inhibit the growth of tumor tissues.

articleTitle: Third Harmonic Generation from Liquid Hemisphere on Silicon Substrate in THz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work third harmonic generation from liquid in terahertz frequency range is addressed. Its generation from a hemisphere of liquid is compared with the one from a layer of water. High generation efficiency is provided by a giant third- order vibrational nonlinearity of water in terahertz frequency range and the fact that the radiation intensity values are high. Spherical lens, formed by a drop of water on a silicon substrate, provides additional enhancement of transmitted radiation.

articleTitle: Modified bow-tie antennas AlGaN/GaN FinFETs for sub-THz detection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the methods of fabrication effective antenna structures for broadband detection by antenna-coupled fin-shaped field-effect transistors (FinFETs) in the terahertz radiation range, using AlGaN/GaN technological process. We demonstrate the efficiency of a split bow-tie antenna solution for a single metal layer design and the way to improve antenna design by FinFET shifting to the middle antenna’s part. Modified bow-tie antennas for FinFETs improve the THz response in the frequency range up to 800 GHz with a maximum of response in the range between 200 GHz and 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Trace Isotope Impurity in Pharmaceutical Material by Terahertz Laser Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Effects of isotope impurity molecule at low content were studied using THz laser spectrometer with high frequency accuracy. D-mannitol crystal was grown controlled to form monoclinic β-form. The lowest absorption peak of such β-form D-mannitol is known to show a very narrow FWHM below 1 GHz. D-sorbitol was added in the range 0.05 to 10.0 % in the solvent before crystallization. Peak frequency shifts of absorption lines of D-mannitol at 10 K on the relation with sorbitol content were evaluated by THz laser spectrometer with high frequency accuracy. It was shown that low content quantitative analysis of isotope impurity was possible.

articleTitle: A FDTD Model Based Coating Thickness Evaluation Using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy in Reflection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A optimization model based on finite difference time domain(FDTD) method is proposed to evaluate accurate coating thickness using terahertz pulse in reflection geometry, which takes into account the multiple reflections caused by Fabry-Perot effect and dispersion of coatings. A deconvolution method with a double Gaussian filter is applied to improve the depth resolution. A stochastic optimization algorithm is used to fit measured signal to simulation signal and improve the robustness of root finding. The proposed method has reached accuracy down to 8μm in single-layer aviation coating samples and can be extended to the multilayer structure easily.

articleTitle: Terahertz Dielectric Transmission Lines: Review and Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this article, we review the terahertz (THz) dielectric transmission lines in recent decade. Moreover, the developed special measurement technologies for measuring the THz dielectric transmission lines are introduced. Final, the various application scenarios of the THz dielectric transmission lines are presented.

articleTitle: Imaging with All-solid-state Electronic Terahertz Device at 330GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The research of active solid-state electronic terahertz (THz) imaging systems have been devoted enormous efforts, which play an important role in nondestructive testing. In this paper, a scanning imaging system based on solid-state electronic modulated THz source at 330GHz is described. To investigate the penetrability of the terahertz waves in this band, we use four kinds of shelters in the experiment. A pyroelectric detector is connected to an oscilloscope to achieve the voltage data which processed by a self-developed imaging data collection and processing system. The imaging results are compared and analyzed to prove the potential of THz waves in the application of target recognition with shelters.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz photoacoustic effect detectable with a microphone
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of photoacoustic signals by irradiating aqueous samples with modulated continuous sub-terahertz waves, which can be detected with a standard microphone. The use of millimeter-waves for excitation and acoustic waves for detection allows us to inspect a sample inside a container through its wall in a non-contact manner. We confirm that the frequency response of the photoacoustic signals is dependent on the sound velocity in the sample, demonstrating its potential for non-contact inspection. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate that the stiffness of gelatin samples can be discerned with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Generation of terahertz vortex beams based on double-arrow-shaped metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a reflective double-arrow-shaped metasurface for generating vortex beams in the terahertz band is proposed. By applying Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase principle, a 2π phase gradient subarray consisted of four cycling units is designed at first, with reflection coefficient over 90%, and smooth phase shifts associated with axis rotation in 0.32-0.36 THz. Hereafter, a 21*21 array is formed with corresponding phase distribution and then effectively converts the circularly polarized waves into second-order vortex beams with a strong orbital angular momentum. This design exhibits the merits of simple structure, broadband bandwidth, and high efficiency.

articleTitle: High-Performance Metal-Grid Polarizers on Polymeric Films for Broadband Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The high-performance broadband terahertz polarizers based on one-dimensional metal grids on carrying thin-film polymeric substrates were developed and manufactured. THz time-domain spectroscopy was used to study their power transmission (PT) and extinction ratio (ER) in the range of 0.2–2 THz. A tandem structure of two polarizers patterned on top of 4-μm-thick polypropylene film showed the best overall characteristics: PT > 95%, while ER exceeded the system dynamic range which spanned from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>:1 to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>:1. The developed polarizers can be used for polarization-sensitive measurements of anisotropic and optically active materials.

articleTitle: A Switchable Terahertz Filter/Absorber based on Graphene and Vanadium Dioxide Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We proposed and demonstrated a switchable terahertz device composed of patterned graphene and vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The device can achieve function switching within the same structure and frequency range. When the graphene Fermi energy level is E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>=0.6 eV and the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in the metal phase, the proposed terahertz device can act as a broadband absorber with the absorption over 90% from 1.15 to 2.13 THz. When the graphene Fermi energy level is E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>=0 eV and the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in the insulator phase, the device can be switched into the broadband filter mode, in which the 3 dB bandwidth is 1.22 THz with the center frequency of 1.58 THz.

articleTitle: 3D-printing conductive periodical structures for application at the THz time-domain spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The article presents the results of research of the electromagnetic properties of 3D-printed periodic conductive composite structures at the frequency range of 0.1 - 1.6 THz. By time-domain spectroscopy the electromagnetic response of 3D-printed samples is obtained. Possibility of using 3D-printed structures as a control element at TDs spectrometer is shown.

articleTitle: Coherent terahertz radiation from waveguide mode excited by an electron beam
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a new mechanism for coherent terahertz radiation. In a dielectric waveguide grating structure, the waveguide mode can by excited by moving electrons, and then resonantly couples with the diffraction waves by the grating to form coherent THz radiation. The resonance greatly narrows the linewidth and enhances the radiation power density at the peak frequency. The radiation frequency can be widely tuned by varying the beam energy or the waveguide thickness. This mechanism could provide a promising way for the development of room temperature, narrow linewidth, high powered, and coherent terahertz radiation source covering the entire terahertz band.

articleTitle: A Monte Carlo Analysis of Double Corrugated Waveguide for a G-band TWT Amplifier Fabricated by UV-LIGA
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Due to the favorable properties like simple topology and compatibility with the cylindrical beam, the double corrugated waveguide is a promising interaction structure for signal amplification and generation at sub-terahertz range. Considerable efforts have been dedicated to deterministic analysis like exploring the dispersion curve for a forward-wave or backward-wave operation. However, the realization of a practical vacuum electronic source concerns also the fabrication process like UV-LIGA, in which multi-dimensional uncertainties are introduced. To quantitatively investigate the sophisticated influences on the final performance resulting from these uncertainties, a Monte Carlo analysis is applied in this work for a G-band amplifier application. The analytic methodology and consequent results are powerful supplements to the conventional design process through taking uncertainties in the unavoidable fabrication process into quantitative consideration.

articleTitle: Effect of Inner Surface Roughness of waveguides on Transmission Performance in Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The influence of high frequency structure’s inner surface roughness on its transmission performance by simulation and modeling in the paper. Taking 0.5THz single grating structure Terahertz backward wave oscillator(BWO) for example, square wave modeling is used as the simulation function of roughness. The results of power loss with those obtained by the calculation method provided in other papers are compared to verify the correctness of the model.

articleTitle: Temperature dependent terahertz spectrum analysis and theoretical calculation of the Dapsone drugs
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dapsone is a sulfonamides drug used to treat various types of leprosy and skin diseases. The temperature dependent absorption spectra of dapsone in the range of 0.3 to2.1THz were obtained. The Gaussian and CASTEP software was used respectively for molecular and crystal calculation of dapsone. The experimental results were compared with the calculated results, and the differences were analyzed in this study.

articleTitle: Extracting the dielectric relaxation of water in thin Nafion membranes by terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) has been demonstrated to be capable of quantifying water uptake and retention properties of Nafion proton exchange membranes (PEMs). With a growing interest in thinner membranes, we analysis thin membranes to reveal its water uptake and retention properties.

articleTitle: Terahertz achromatic quarter-wave plate composed of quartz and MgF2
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain polarimetry is a useful tool to study the polarization property of an object in a broadband frequency range. Waveplate is the core component of polarimetry. An achromatic quarter-wave plate consists of a quartz plate and a MgF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plate with low absorbance is proposed. The thickness and the orientation with respect to the optical axis of each plate were calculated by simulated annealing algorithm. The resulting retardation of the achromatic quarter-wave plate works in the frequency range of 0.7 – 1.6 THz with the dephasing error of 3%. The theoretical transmittance of the waveplate is also provided and compared with conventional achromatic waveplate made of quartz.

articleTitle: THz phase waveplates for beam shaping
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Phase waveplates for THz beam shaping were developed, calculated, and implemented. Developed phase plates could be 3D-printed from commercially available polymers, which makes them affordable and fully customized. These waveplates allow to widely and easily manipulate THz beam shape.

articleTitle: 140-GHz Low-Loss Wideband Air-Filled Waveguide Transition Integrated in LTCC and The Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Air-filled waveguide integrated in Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) has advantages of low loss and high efficiency compared with the SIW using dielectric substrate-filled waveguide and is suitable for the design of sub-millimeter wave and terahertz circuits and components. In this paper, a 140 GHz low-loss integrated air-filled waveguide is designed in LTCC, and to feed the integrated air-filled waveguide, a wideband transition from metal rectangular waveguide to LTCC air-filled waveguide is presented using a stage impedance matching structure based on the LTCC manufacture process technology. Moreover, a horn antenna integrated in LTCC is designed at 140-GHz band and fed by the low-loss integrated air-filled waveguide. To obtain higher gain, a dielectric loaded SIW stage horn antenna is designed. The transition and antenna show good performance and demonstrate the application potential over the sub-millimeter wave and terahertz frequencies of integrated air-filled waveguide in LTCC.

articleTitle: Information Metamaterials and Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metamaterials have great capabilities and flexibilities in controlling electromagnetic (EM) waves since their subwavelength meta-atoms can be designed and tailored in desired ways. However, once the structure-only metamaterials (i.e., passive metamaterials) are fabricated, their functions will be fixed. To control the EM waves dynamically, some active devices are integrated into the meta-atoms, yielding active metamaterials. Traditionally, the active metamaterials include tunable metamaterials and reconfigurable metamaterials, which have either small-range tunability or a few numbers of reconfigurability. Recently, a special kind of active metamaterials, digital coding and programmable metamaterials, have been presented, which can realize a large number of distinct functionalities and switch them in real time with the aid of field programmable gate array. More importantly, the digital coding representations of metamaterials make it possible to bridge the digital world and physical world using the metamaterial platform, and make the metamaterials process digital information directly, resulting in information metamaterials. In this regard, the information metamaterial is no longer an effective material or medium, but an information system. In this presentation, I will firstly introduce the evolution of metamaterials, and then present the concepts and basic principles of digital coding metamaterials and information metamaterials. With more details, I will introduce a series of information metamaterial systems, including the programmable meta-systems, software meta-systems, and intelligent meta-systems. Particularly, I will present two important applications of the information metamaterials: intelligent computational imaging and wireless communications.

articleTitle: Waveforms with High Spectral Efficiency for Terahertz Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a pulse shape design that fully complies with the spectral emission requirements of the IEEE 802.15.3d Standard. The proposed pulse shape offers up to two orders of magnitude of improvement in the bit error rate performance compared to the conventional raised-cosine pulse.

articleTitle: Characterization of Building Materials for THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The future communication systems is naturally evolving towards higher carrier frequencies in order to satisfy the increasing demand for higher data rates. We investigate the dielectric and scattering properties of building materials across the THz band. This information will be of use to model indoor THz communication environments.

articleTitle: Ultra-high coercivity and terahertz ferromagnetic resonance in single-domain hexaferrite nano-ceramics
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Record values of natural ferromagnetic resonance frequency up to 250 GHz and of coercive force up to 36 kOe were obtained in Ca-Al substituted strontium hexaferrite nano-ceramics. Variation of annealing time was shown to affect the magnetic properties and particle size of the ceramic materials.

articleTitle: Undulator Amplification of a Long Sub-Terahertz Wave Signal by a Short Dense Electron Bunch
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Amplification of a long THz-frequency-range wave pulse coming from a continuous-wave gyrotron by a short electron bunch is studied in the situation, when the axial electron velocity is close to the wave group velocity. The possibility of realization of two different regimes of the electron-wave interaction at different slippages between the electron bunch and the wave is shown. In the case of a short bunch and the zero slippage, a quasi-regular amplification is possible; in this regime, the amplitude increases in a region around the moving bunch and, therefore, a wave pulse with a relatively long length (as compared to the electron bunch length) is formed. The second regime is realized in the case when the bunch is relatively long, and it slightly slips with respect to the wave. In this case, a short (as compared to the bunch length) wave pulse is formed on one of fronts of the bunch and amplifies as it "runs" along the bunch. The peak power of this wave pulse can be several orders of magnitude higher than the saturated power achieved in the quasi-regular amplification regime.

articleTitle: Selective Excitation of Symmetric Modes in Gyrotrons with Azimuthally-Asymmetric Cavities
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An electrodynamic method based on azimuthally asymmetric cavities is proposed to provide selective excitation of symmetric TE waves in fundamental-harmonic gyrotrons. The presence of small azimuthal inhomogeneities in a cavity with a "close-to-circular" cross-section does not affect on excitation of the operating TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,p</inf> mode, but increases the starting current of excitation of the parasitic TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,p</inf> mode. This approach can ensure also mechanical adjustment of the frequency of the operating TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,p</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Stable terahertz in-situ photo-writable electrically-erasable memory with CsPbI3:Ag/SnO2/PEDOT:PSS hybrid structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Stable terahertz photo-writable electrical-erasable memory from CsPbI3:Ag (Ag-nanoparticles added CsPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/PEDOT:PSS hybrid sample was investigated. Significant THz modulation depth of CsPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>:Ag/PEDOT:PSS was obtained with low optical excitation intensity. After the insertion of a SnO2 film between the CsPbI3 and PEDOT:PSS, a 34% terahertz modulation depth was reached under optical excitation, and the recovery time of modulated THz transmission was considerably prolonged on removal of laser excitation. On applying a bias voltages to the CsPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>:Ag/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/PEDOT:PSS structure, THz transmission were quickly returned. THz transmissions were apply to be coded pixel units and were programmed to store image signal. Based on this, a stable photo-memory functionality was accomplished with the CsPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>:Ag/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/PEDOT:PSS composite sample using a method for in situ electrically-erasing information stored in both the spectrum and image.

articleTitle: Spontaneous Emission of Broadband Terahertz Wave Pulses by Short Dense Electron Bunches
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spontaneous coherent super-radiative emission in the terahertz frequency range from a short dense electron bunch is studied for various regimes. If the wave group velocity is close to the bunch velocity, this is a process of spontaneous radiation followed by amplification of a single wave cycle. Despite the Coulomb repulsion of electrons inside the bunch, a short length of the bunch needed to ensure the spontaneous coherent character of the radiation is provided by the self-compression of the bunch under the action of its radiation fields. The additional compression can be provided by the use of the negative-mass regime of the electron motion in the undulator with strong axial magnetic field. As a result, formation of an ultra-short (several cycles) wave packet occurs, when the bunch moves through several undulator periods with high (~10%) efficiency of extraction of the electron energy and high intensity (up to several hundred MV/m) of the peak wave field.

articleTitle: Waveguide integrated terahertz quantum-cascade laser systems
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed precision micromachining techniques for integration of terahertz quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) with waveguides and feedhorns for use as local oscillators in satellite-borne receivers. We demonstrate these techniques using QCLs at 3.4 THz and 4.7 THz, as well as the first QCL with a monolithically integrated power modulator.

articleTitle: Large-aperture, manually-poled LiNbO3 and KTP for efficient, narrowband THz generation
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Large-aperture, manually-poled LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> wafers have already been used to generate THz radiation. However, the results were limited to room-temperature operation with only a few cycles. Here, we extend the number of cycles and improve the efficiency by increasing the number of wafers and using another non-linear material, KTP, at cryogenic nitrogen temperature.

articleTitle: Observation of Layer Dependent Ultrafast Carrier dynamics and Interlayer Coherent Phonon Dynamics in PdSe2 Films
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, by employing ultrafast optical pump-probe spectroscopy, we investigated the photocarrier dynamics as well as the thickness dependent interlayer coherent phonon modes in PdSe2 films. Two low-frequency phonon modes in PdSe2 films are identified after photoexcitation at 780 nm. The higher frequency mode is ascribed to the interlayer breathing mode, and the lower one is assigned to the standing wave mode, and the frequency variation and the related parameters (interlayer force constant and sound velocity) of the two modes are investigated.

articleTitle: Powerful W-band Planar Cherenkov Maser with 2D Slow-Wave Structure: Conceptual Design and Recent Results
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Project of GW-power W-band planar Cherenkov oscillator driven by large-size sheet electron beam forming by the "ELMI" accelerator 1 MeV / 5 -7 kA / 3 µs is under development in collaboration between IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) and BINP RAS (Novosibirsk). Electrodynamic system of this maser is based on 2D periodical slow-wave structure realizing 2D distributed feedback mechanism and allowing for provision of stable narrow-band oscillation regime under conditions of substantial oversize. Design parameters, key components and results of simulations of this oscillator are presented, status of its experimental realization is discussed.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband electrical terahertz modulator based on metal microslits and n-doped GaAs formed Schottky diode
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An ultrabroadband electrical terahertz modulator exploited periodic metal microslits on n-GaAs layer forming a Schottky diode structure was proposed and demonstrated. The carrier concentration between the gap of microslits in the n-GaAs layer was modified by an external reverse bias voltage, which enabled effective modulation of the transmitted THz signal in a broad bandwidth. Our proof of principle device achieved an intensity modulation depth of ~45% by changing bias voltage between 0 and -5 volts. Further optimization, such as the free carrier density and parameters of the microslits, may further improve the device performance.

articleTitle: Efficient and Optically-Controlled Phase Modulator Based on VO2 EIT Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dynamic EIT meta-surface to achieve large phase modulation of THz waves with low-loss. The dynamic EIT meta-surface is composed of a metallic coupled EIT meta-array and the embed vanadium dioxide components. By changing the state of VO2, the EIT resonant mode can be converted into a dipolar resonant. During this process, the transmitted frequency peak could be changed to a forbidden peak so that a 90-degree phase shift with low-loss at 0.6THz and 0.68THz frequency is obtained.

articleTitle: Terahertz harmonic mixer based on HTS Josephson junction
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: High temperature superconducting (HTS) Josephson junction (JJ) mixers are attractive candidates in receivers for terahertz (THz) communication due to their high sensitivity, wide bandwidth, low local oscillator (LO) power requirement and high harmonic numbers. The required LO frequencies and the cost can be greatly reduced when harmonic signals can be detected at high orders (more than 100). In this paper, up to 114<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic mixings is presented in a HTS bicrystal YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-δ</inf> (YBCO) JJ harmonic mixer coupled with a bowtie loaded meander antenna at 0.21 THz. HTS JJs will be promising high-order harmonic mixers for THz practical applications on reception or detection at THz bands.

articleTitle: A 170-GHz Modulator Based on Doule Schottky Diodes with Differential-Feed Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we present a 170-GHz modulator combined with series Schottky diodes and microstructure with differential-feed technique. The diodes are controlled by the bias voltage to change the switching characteristics. Then, the resonant mode is controlled to realize the amplitude modulation of THz (terahertz) waves. The simulation results indicate that the modulator can achieve an insertion loss of 2dB and a maximum modulation depth of 17dB.

articleTitle: Design of W-band Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) by utilizing the folded waveguide slow wave structure (FWSWS) combined with the pencil beam is designed to develop the high power millimeter-wave radiation source. The particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that this TWT can produce over 158W output power in the range from 90GHz to 97GHz. The maximum output power of the TWT can reach 293W at the typical frequency of 94GHz, which corresponds to a gain of 37.68dB and an interaction efficiency of 8.15%.

articleTitle: Telecom-compatible LTG-GaAs Photoconductive Antenna Modules with more than 85 dB Peak Dynamic Range
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present robust terahertz emitter and detector modules, based on LTG-GaAs photoconductive antennas with nonlinear second-harmonic generation for the use in 1550 nm terahertz time-domain spectroscopy systems. With two different dipole antenna-structures with 20 µm and 60 µm dipole length, the spectral performance of pitch-catch transceivers is adjustable. We achieve peak dynamic ranges of up to 87.7 dB and bandwidths of more than 5.5 THz for 5 minutes integration time.

articleTitle: Dual substrate lenses on TeraFET detector enable Fourier imaging based on sub-harmonic detection at 600 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 3D THz imaging system based on the coherent recording of the Fourier-space spectrum at 600 GHz by sub-harmonic heterodyne detection at 300 GHz is presented. The instrument uses a broad-band Si CMOS TeraFET mixer between two substrate lenses (one made from silicon, the other from PTFE) which increase the coupling efficiency of both the signal and the local oscillator (LO) radiation to the detector. Applying subharmonic detection combines the advantages of a high spatial resolution (at 600 GHz) and limited costs for the LO.

articleTitle: Subwavelength silicon terahertz optics for generation of coherent beams with pre-given polarization state
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Coherent terahertz beams with radial polarization of 1,2 and 3 orders have been generated by the use of silicon subwavelength diffractive optical elements (DOEs). The beam of terahertz Novosibirsk Free Electron Laser was used as the illuminating beam. Experimental results are in good agreement with the results of computer simulation.

articleTitle: Helix Slow-wave Structure with Changed Pitches for a Q-band Traveling-wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a helix slow-wave structure (SWS) with changed pitches for a Q-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) is proposed. Changed pitches are used to achieve more sufficient beam-wave interaction in the SWS. The high frequency characteristics and beam-wave interaction of the Q-band TWT are analyzed by using CST. The voltage standing wave ratio is less than 1.5 from 39 to 42 GHz. The simulation results of the beam-wave interaction show that the Q-band TWT with the changed pitches can generate output power of more than 80 W and electronic efficiency of 14% in the operating frequency band. The electronic efficiency reaches the maximum of 16.09% at 39 GHz.

articleTitle: Investigation of 340GHz 10W Modified Sine Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The development of a 340GHz modified sine waveguide vacuum electron amplifier is presented here. Output power from this structure is predicated to exceed 10W with a pencil beam electron gun at 17 kV and 38mA. Design, fabrication and test of slow wave structure (SWS) and pillbox window are discussed respectively. The cold test results show a good agreement with the simulation, which verified the properties of low loss and wide bandwidth of the high frequency system.

articleTitle: Optical control of terahertz plasmon-induced transparency based on hybrid CdSe nanoplates metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The effective interaction between light and matter is explored by integrating photosensitive materials into structured metamaterials. In this work, the CdSe nanoplates are incorporated into the metasurfaces, realizing active control of the plasmoninduced transparency. The experimental results show that the transparent window is significantly modulated from 0.67 to 0.378. The combination of nanoplates and metasurfaces provides a new idea for active terahertz devices.

articleTitle: Investigations of a high gain W-band gyro-TWA
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical investigation of alternate gyrotron Traveling Wave Amplifier (gyro-TWA) configurations for increased gain. Previous experimental results showed a maximum stable gain of 37 dB over the frequency range 90-96 GHz. These results were limited in bandwidth by the input power from the solid-state pre-amplifier. The simplest way to mitigate the limited input power available is to increase amplifier gain. Doing so without inducing instability requires the introduction of losses to the RF circuit. We present PIC simulations contrasting a range of new designs combining two gain stages and lossy elements with results for the single section design presented in our earlier experimental program.

articleTitle: A Superfocusing Plasmonic Plate with Physically Achievable Extreme Sizes
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Based on the effect of radiationless electromagnetic interference (REI), a dual-foci superfocusing is achieved using a plasmonic array with a physically realizable extreme size of 0.195λ, where λ is the free-space wavelength). The full widths at half maximum (FWHM) of both electric and magnetic fields are 0.061λ and 0.052λ at a distance of 0.1λ.

articleTitle: Mid-IR lasing up to 260 K in HgCdTe/CdHgTe QW structure with microdisk resonators under optical pumping
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on lasing up to 5.1 μm in an array of microdisk resonators of various sizes (5 – 40 μm in diameter) formed from the waveguide heterostructure with multiple HgCdTe/CdHgTe quantum wells (QWs). The lasing was observed at temperatures as high as 260 K, which is achievable with thermoelectric cooling. FWHM of laser line at 100 K was less than 1 meV, which is several times lower than FWHM of single-pass stimulated emission line obtained from the same structure without microdisk resonators processed.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Band Transceiver with Agile Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a terahertz band transceiver with agile beam steering is proposed. The system works in 220GHz frequency band and consists of double feed horns and a shared reflector. It transmits a single frequency at 216GHz, and receives from 213GHz-219GHz except 216GHz. Test results show that the switching time between two beams of the terahertz agile beam-steering system is only ~30ns.

articleTitle: Magnetron Injection Gun for an 800 GHz Pulsed Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper proposes the design and preliminary experiment of a magnetron injection gun (MIG) for an 800 GHz gyrotron operating with a 15T pulsed magnet. The triode type MIG design is performed to control beam parameters for the fundamental harmonic operation (400 GHz) and the second harmonic operation (800 GHz). A pitch factor of 1.3 and a transverse velocity spread of 2.29% were obtained under a 400 mA beam current. With the proposed MIG, the terahertz waves of 383.75 GHz and 803.7 GHz are detected in the experiment.

articleTitle: Photo-excited terahertz response of topological insulator Sb2Te3
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: By employing ultrafast time-resolved optical pump terahertz (THz) probe spectroscopy, we report a comparative THz response on CVD grown topological insulator (TI) Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> under different temperatures. Both photo induced carrier dynamics attributed to the surface and bulk electrons are observed. The electron system undergoes an ultrafast excitation and relaxation and releases through intra-band and inter-band scattering.

articleTitle: Electrical detection of terahertz radiation by silicon carbide nanostructure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The ability to detect the terahertz (THz) emission from a silicon nanosandwich structure (Si-NS) is demonstrated with the silicon carbide nanostructure (SiC-NS) as a detector. Electrical response in longitudinal voltage of the detector was observed under the constant drain-source current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds(DET)</inf>) of the detector.

articleTitle: Controlling the Permittivities and Permeabilities of Epoxy/Silver Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The electromagnetic properties of materials are generally frequency-dependent. Controlling the permittivities and the permeabilities of composites are commonly achieved in a narrow frequency range. This work characterizes the electromagnetic properties of the epoxy/silver nanocomposites using transmission/reflection method. The silver nanoparticles serving as electric dipoles enhance the permittivity as the volume fraction increases. On the other hand, the rapidly changing magnetic field induces current on the conducting silver particles resulting in a negative polarizability. The macroscopic magnetic susceptivities are negative under the long-wavelength limit. The electromagnetic properties are controllable and just slightly change over a very broad frequency range from 8 GHz to 110 GHz.

articleTitle: Sensing Accuracy Improvement of an OFDM W-band System
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to improve the sensing accuracy of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform, based on estimation of delay/Doppler leakages in the channel matrix. Both simulation and proof-of-concept experiment are implemented, and the ranging accuracy improvement is validated in a W-band system, making the proposed approach promising in driving the convergence of OFDM-based sensing and communications.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Nonlinear Carrier Dynamics in n-Doped Ge at High Field Strengths
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ultrafast carrier dynamics in n-doped Ge is investigated by THz pump—THz probe spectroscopy with pump THz field strengths up to <0.45 MV/cm provided by a user-accessible compact nonlinear THz spectroscopy facility at ELI-ALPS. The saturation and recovery of the free-carrier absorption is observed on picosecond time scale at 300 K and 95 K temperatures. Furthermore, the intensity-dependent modulation of the refractive index is also observed.

articleTitle: Terahertz Dynamics of Sodium Silicate Glass Investigated by Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We performed terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, low-frequency Raman scattering and low-temperature specific heat measurements to investigate different compositions of sodium silicate glasses. The boson peak (BP) behavior was successfully detected in all measurements. The BP frequency was found to be insensitive to Na2O composition. Additionally, comparing the Raman spectrum and terahertz absorption spectrum confirmed that the BP vibration mode is a combination of different fundamental vibration modes.

articleTitle: Microwave Pyrolysis of Peat: Optimization of Oversized Reactor and Experimental Results
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The paper presents the results of microwave pyrolysis of a peat in the oversized reactor powered by an industrial magnetron at a frequency of 2.45 GHz and a power level of 1 kW. The components of the RF pyrolysis complex have been upgraded to ensure its continuous operation. Samples of the gas, liquid, and solid phases were obtained and analyzed using the optimized set-up.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic sub-THz emission from a beam-plasma system with oblique density modulations
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Recent experiments on the injection of kiloampere electron beams into a magnetized plasma at the GOL-PET facility have shown that the power of sub-terahertz radiation escaping from the plasma along the magnetic field increases by more than an order of magnitude if strong radial density gradients are preliminarily created in the plasma. In this work, we study effects of the different periodic density modulations on electromagnetic emission from the plasma. First, PIC simulations were performed with the strong transverse density gradient measured in the experiment. They did not show considerable increase in electromagnetic emission relative to the case of the uniform plasma. However, a small oblique modulation of the plasma density $n = {n_0} + \Delta n \cdot \cos (\vec q \cdot \vec r)$ with $\Delta n \sim 0.05{n_0}$ makes it possible to obtain the power of the output radiation at the level of 1-3% of the beam power due to the antenna mechanism. This mechanism has been previously found to be effective only in a thin plasma with the radial size comparable with the radiation wavelength. In this work, based on analytical and simulation studies, we discuss how efficiently this mechanism can work in a thick plasma typical to GOL-PET experiments.

articleTitle: Terahertz response of Bi-substituted rare-earth iron garnet
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The terahertz optical and magneto-optical response of Bi-substituted rare-earth iron garnet film were studied from 0.2 to 1.2 THz. The thickness of film is 406 μm. The maximum transmittance is over 55% near the frequency point of 0.35 THz. When the external magnetic field change from -100 mT to +100 mT, the Faraday rotation angle is between -5° and +7°. Large Verdet constants approaching 270 °/T/mm are found. The overall change of ellipticity is relatively small.

articleTitle: An Efficient 400 GHz Active Multiplier-Based Signal Source for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a 400 GHz signal source using a 0.8 μm transferred substrate (TS) InP-HBT technology. The signal source is based on an active balanced doubler and delivers -4.5 dBm peak output power at 374 GHz, with a DC consumption of only 7 mW, which corresponds to 5 % conversion efficiency. It achieves more than 60 GHz bandwidth. The core chip area of the source covers only 0.7 x 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Quasi-Optical Mode Converter for 0.5THz-TE8,5 Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper a quasi-optical mode converter (QOMC) consists of a hybrid-type launcher and two phase-correcting mirrors is presented, which is used for a 0.5THz-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8,5</inf> gyrotron. The results show that the gyrotron operating mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8,5</inf> is radiated into free space by the launcher and focused by two phase-correcting mirrors. Finally, a quasi-Gaussian wave beam is formed at the output window. The scalar and vector Gaussian mode content of the final output wave are about 99.7% and 99.0%, respectively.

articleTitle: Asymmetric-Structure Modification of Terahertz All-Dielectric Metamaterial for Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Analogue with High-Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An all-dielectric metamaterial (ADMM) based on asymmetric split-ring resonator (A-SRR) is proposed and numerically demonstrated in the terahertz range. The coupling between a bright mode supported by the silicon bars and a dark mode supported by the A-SRR leads to an analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). By simply modifying the symmetric SRR into the asymmetric structure, the quality factor of the EIT peak can significantly increase from 255 to 1410, exhibiting a better slow-light performance. This work gives a new way to adjust the asymmetry of the ADMM for higher quality factor, which is useful for applications in slow-light devices and chemical/biological sensors.

articleTitle: Influence of Optical Rectification on Terahertz Generation from Plasma Induced by Two-color Pulses
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The influence of optical rectification on terahertz radiation driven by two-color laser pulses has been determined quantitatively, by the crucial factors including the BBO crystal rotation angle, the pump power, and the numerical aperture of the focusing lens. The experimental and simulation results show that the above factors have dramatically affected the intensity ratio of the THz waves from the plasma and BBO crystal. It renews the understanding of the THz wave generation from two-color-plasma.

articleTitle: Sensitive Ultrafast Dynamic Spectroscopy of OH Radicals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The OH radical is a short-lived intermediate component in many important chemical reactions. The Novosibirsk free electron laser (NovoFEL) makes it possible to measure ultrafast spectral cinema of dynamics of this radical. In this paper, methods of increasing the sensitivity of such measurements by using a weak magnetic field and a heterodyne scheme are considered.

articleTitle: Angle-independent beam splitter based on spoof surface plasmon
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we propose an angle-independent beam splitter based on spoof surface plasmon. Arbitrary incident waves can be divided in half, and scatter towards two specific and independent directions. The proposed beam splitter consists of the upper periodic metal cylinder and the metal grating below. The former is placed to modulate the incident wave and the spoof surface plasmon with the specified wave vector, and the latter is used to support the excited spoof surface plasmon. To verify the proposed functionalities, we design three beam splitters with different splitter angles and calculate their field distributions under the illumination of the same Gaussian beam. The ideal numerical results agree well with the theory.

articleTitle: A Terahertz s-SNOM tip with integrated photoconductive emitter switch evaluated on an AFM-system platform
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate time-domain THz scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (THz sSNOM) with local pulsed THz generation close to the scattering tip that could overcome performance limitations of the commonly used THz far-field excitation scheme.

articleTitle: 252-GHz Compact All-Electronic CMOS Optopair with SNR of 62 dB
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A free space 252 GHz quasi-optical emitter-detector pair (optopair) is implemented in standard Si CMOS technology. The THz source consists of a voltage-controlled differential field-effect-transistor (FET) based Colpitts oscillator emitting at the third harmonic with total radiated power -11.1 dBm and 35 mW DC power consumption. The detector is a resonant-antenna-coupled FET-based power detector for quasi-optic coupling through the substrate lens. The detector exhibits a minimum optical noise equivalent power as low as $22{\text{pW}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $ at 252 GHz. The system reveals 61.7 dB power signal to noise for 1 Hz equivalent noise bandwidth in the direct detection regime. The practical application of the pair for two-dimensional imaging is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Radiation pattern of photodiode based bowtie antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Photodiode based emitters are established for continuous-wave terahertz spectroscopy and highly relevant for future wireless communication due to seamless integration in fiber-optical networks. For both applications, the directivity and the beam profile are of major interest. We investigated the radiation pattern experimentally between 100 GHz and 500 GHz. Radiation properties can be linked directly to the antenna structure due to the identical packaging and material of all emitters. We observed a large influence of the feeding point structure that connects photodiode and antenna. We demonstrate a new antenna with increased directivity and lower side lobes.

articleTitle: Characters of frequency response of TM mode with the Tapered Double Sinusoidal Grooves structure operating at 0.35THz frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In order to construct a cavity with a high-frequency and high-order single TM operating mode and also are favorable to the mode selectivity, the tapered double sinusoidal grooves structure is proposed. On the basis of ordinary sinusoidal grooves structure, the auxiliary sinusoidal distribution with smaller etching period is superimposed, and the taper is added on the inner and outer conductor walls to form the tapered double sinusoidal grooves coaxial Bragg structure. Through the FORTRAN software programming simulation experiments, we can see that it is different from the working mode TE mode. When the positive taper double sinusoidal grooves is adopted, the band gap overlap phenomenon deteriorates. The use of negative taper double sinusoidal grooves coaxial Bragg structure as the reflector can effectively suppress the band gap overlap phenomenon, the bandwidth gradually becomes wider as the increase of the taper angle, and the working mode TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62</inf> and the competition mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">61</inf> can further separate. This provides a theoretical reference for the design of a coaxial Bragg reflector with a high-frequency and high-order single TM operating mode.

articleTitle: Perimeter Dependence of Oscillation Frequency Property of Resonant Tunneling Diode Terahertz Oscillator Using Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Resonant tunneling diode (RTD) terahertz oscillator without a metal–insulator–metal (MIM) capacitor offers easy deployment. Here, we propose RTD oscillators using different perimeters of square split ring resonators (SRRs) without MIM capacitors. The RTD is integrated into the center split gap of the SRR. Coplanar stripline antennas are integrated with the SRR to increase the output power. The highest measured oscillation frequency is 1.22 THz with an output power of ~7 µW.

articleTitle: Detecting capacity of THz method applied to art painting
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we have obtained terahertz images of hidden signatures that were located on the back side of the test-object’s canvas and covered by covered with a thick layer of brown paint. It was demonstrated that in the tomogram obtained at a frequency of 0.3-0.5 THz, the layers of paint applied on the other side of canvas are clearly distinguishable.

articleTitle: Effect of CW laser illumination on Fe-doped β-Ga2O3
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gallium oxide are a potential material for many applications and recent research showed its strong anisotropic properties in THz range. We applied THz-TDS and CW laser to study the excited carrier dynamics in our sample (Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, 010, Fe-doped). The results showed different response along two crystal axes. Along the a-axis we observed Drude response and conductivity are increasing with CW laser increasing, as the same as we expected. Our fitting results (by Drude model) of this direction also agreed with our expectation. Along the c-axis we observed non-Drude response and further experiments are needed.

articleTitle: Directly observing charge-transfer free carriers in 2D MoS2/ReSe2 monolayer heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures offer a new platform to engineer the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. Large scale heterostructures of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and ReSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monolayers were fabricated and fully investigated using time-resolved terahertz (THz) spectroscopy (TRTS), THz emission spectroscopy, and optical pump-probe spectroscopy (OPPS). The charge transfer (CT) time was estimated to be 170 fs by fitting the photocurrent model to the emitted THz pulse. In TRTS, free carrier dominated dynamic has been unambiguous investigated. In addition, it is found that interlayer and intralayer excitons are dominant in carrier dynamics before and after CT saturation in the OPPS. The intriguing results pave the way for further understanding the ultrafast carrier relaxation dynamics in 2D heterostructures and potential applications in opto-electronic devices.

articleTitle: Investigating Implantation Damage of Hyperdoped Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Hyperdoping semiconductor is one of the material candidates for intermediate band photovoltaics. We investigate implantation damage and associated defects. Time resolved terahertz spectroscopy reveals that charge carrier lifetime is hindered by defects not detected by conventional microscopic and spectroscopic techniques.

articleTitle: W-band waveguide embedded nanofiber absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel type of absorber integrate into a standard WR-10 metal waveguide of is developed and measured. The absorber is based on alumina nanofibers covered with single or multi- carbon layers. Employing this technique for the CNT based absorbers offers a material with micron scales-oriented 3D microstructures, that is hybrid alumina nanofibers covered with carbon layer. These microstructures result in a low level of reflectance and good absorbance at 75-110 GHz frequency band due to the highly porous and low conductivity.

articleTitle: Laser Terahertz Emission Microscope as a Killer Tool
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A laser terahertz emission microscope (LTEM) will be a killer tool as a real-world application. Here various examples are reviewed to prove it.

articleTitle: Up to 100 Gbit/s short link using 300 GHz band Yagi-Uda antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the use of a Yagi-Uda antenna on polymer substrate used for indoor 300 GHz data-link applications. The Yagi-Uda antenna-based data-link is validated for up to QAM-16 signals (100 Gbit/s).

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband modulator based on broken dispersion of spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper,an ultra-wideband modulator is designed by destroying the dispersion characteristics of spoof surface plasmon polaritons on the grating embedded by vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). When the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is on the dielectric state, the boundary condition is changed, which leads to a broken of the SSPPs dispersion, resulting in dramatically amplitude modulation. The results show an excellent isolation effect up to 40 dB in a large bandwith of 120 GHz with an insertion loss better than -1 dB.

articleTitle: Generation of THz transients in FeCo/graphene nanobilayers by femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate generation of time-resolved THz transients in a FeCo/graphene nanobilayer, excited by femtosecond optical laser pulses. The signal sign dependency on the experimental geometry and the external magnetic field allows assigning the mechanism of the THz radiation to the inverse spin Hall effect with a spin-to-charge current conversation parameter of the order of 0.001 nm.

articleTitle: THz Biosensor Based on Metasurface Integrated with Spintronic Emitter
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Currently spintronic THz sources have the advantages of low cost, high efficiency, and easy integration, so it can be used to integrate feature-rich devices. In this paper, we demonstrate the function of THz sensing by metasurface integrated with spintronic THz emitter. Through electromagnetic simulation, the resonant frequency point of metasurface was designed to be around 0.8 THz. Then the metasurface was fabricated on a quartz substrate and shared the substrate with a spintronic emitter. This integrated THz biosensor was used to measure the transmittance spectra of water, alcohol and olive oil. The experimental results show that it is sensitive for identifying different liquids according to the frequency shift.

articleTitle: Terahertz Radiation from a Thin GaAs Crystal in a Metallic Tapered Parallel Plate Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz generation in a thin (100-µm thick) GaAs crystal sandwiched between the walls of a metallic tapered parallel plate waveguide at its narrow end and pumped by a 1560-nm femtosecond laser has been experimentally studied. The terahertz radiation characteristics are compared with those from a thick bulk GaAs crystal in a free space. The results demonstrate that the taper structure improves the directivity of terahertz emission from thin crystals pumped by focused optical beams.

articleTitle: Fiber Coupled THz Time-Domain Spectrometer with 10 THz Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a fiber coupled THz time-domain spectrometer exhibiting a record bandwidth of 10 THz. This significant increase in bandwidth was enabled by improving the photoconductive antennas (PCAs) used as THz emitter and receiver. In particular, we identified absorption in the InP:Fe substrate of the PCAs as the main limiting factor for the spectral bandwidth. To minimize this absorption, we developed a wafer-scale substrate transfer process for the thin photoconductive InGaAs layer from the InP:Fe substrate onto a low-loss, high-resistivity float-zone Si substrate. Hence, our work shows a promising path towards ultrabroadband fiber coupled THz TDS systems.

articleTitle: Terahertz transitions in n-type Ge/SiGe Parabolic Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Ge/SiGe heterostructures are promising in the view of silicon-foundry compatible THz optoelectronic applications. Here we present a structural and optical characterization of Ge/SiGe parabolic quantum wells that represent ideal systems for room-temperature THz emission and strong light-matter coupling investigation.

articleTitle: A 140GHz terahertz modulator based on a fin line structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a modulator based on a fin line structure is designed to change the electric state of the diode switch, It uses differential voltage to realize the on-off of the terahertz wave, to implement the modulation of the terahertz signal. It can be achieved in a 140GHz band, the modulation depth of more than 20dB, bandwidth up to 15GHz.

articleTitle: A tunable ultra-wideband planar metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a tunable outer square inner circle coupled metamaterial absorber for planar microwave circuits, which is parallel to the electromagnetic wave transmission direction. The tunable ultra-wideband absorption is achieved by loading electrorheological fluid with electrically tunable permittivity in metamaterial absorber. The simulation results show that the absorption of the absorber reaches up to 90% from 31.92 GHz to 81.76 GHz. The absorption band gradually shifts to lower frequency with the increasing of electric field strength applied on electrorheological fluid, which starts from 31.92 GHz and moves to 26.32GHz when electric field strength applied from 0 V/mm to 816 V/mm. Moreover, the upper frequency of the 90% wideband almost no change with the electric field strength.

articleTitle: Terahertz near-field microscopy with a fast quantum-well photodetector
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on a scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscope (s-SNOM) based on a terahertz quantum cascade laser (QCL) and a fast terahertz quantum-well photodetector (QWP). The natural polarization of terahertz QWP and terahertz QCL can improve the coupling efficiency. A resolution of about 60 nm is obtained.

articleTitle: Beam Steering for Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy Using Optical Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we circumvent the bandwidth limitation of an optical ring resonator (ORR) as a delay element by exploiting the periodicity of its group delay response and simulate wideband beam steering for terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) driven by a mode-locked laser diode (MLLD). First, we derive the transfer matrix of a Mach-Zehnder modulator-based ORR and calculate the delays that the ORRs in the photonic beam steering network introduce to the individual laser modes. Second, we use the delayed laser pulses in a simulation of a ten-element array. In the simulation, the resulting terahertz beam is successfully steered in the desired direction without any beam squint across a bandwidth of 1 THz.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Ice Covers by Low Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Under adverse outdoor weather conditions, road surface is often covered by ice or snow, which usually leads to deceasing of friction between automotive tires and road surface. This would degrade transportation efficiency and driving safety seriously. Monitoring of ice or snow covers on road surface becomes necessary and important for reduction of traffic accident rate. In this work, we propose to employ terahertz frequencies to recognize surface conditions (such as roughness and thickness) of a soil road covered by ice. A theoretical model combining surface and volume scattering mechanisms is conducted. Good agreement between the calculation results and measured data confirms the efficiency of low THz frequencies for ice surface monitoring with higher resolution.

articleTitle: Cellulose nanofibers doped with conductive nanomaterials for THz applications
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cellulose-based materials have shown a variety of attractive properties in the past few years. Here, we characterized the THz properties of biomimetic aerogels based on cellulose nanofibers doped with various conductive materials, carbon nanotubes, silver nanowires, and MXene. The differently doped cellulose samples demonstrate a low refractive index as well as high birefringence and absorption, making these materials candidates for future THz optical devices such as THz polarizers and waveplates. In addition, the complex refractive index of MXene is estimated.

articleTitle: Method to decrease ohmic losses in cavities of low-power terahertz gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In sub-THz and THz gyrotrons with oversized cavities, there is the problem of implementation of stable single-mode generation in modes, operating at high cyclotron harmonics. It is shown that a high fraction of ohmic losses in sub-THz and THz gyrotrons affects not only the efficiency and output power, but also affects the stability of the operating regime.
