abstract: An efficient Fourier optics method for synthesizing a required incident beam to compute the internal and scattered electromagnetic fields from known spherical surface electric field distribution is presented.

articleTitle: The Response Wavelength Modulation of Terahertz Detector based on Metal Gratings/Si Blocked-impurity-band Hybrid Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz band detection technology is widely researched, for it brings chemical composition and material quality information of the object. In this work, the metal gratings/Si Blocked-impurity-band (BIB) hybrid structure is proposed. Then, we fabricate two devices with different metallic gratings and one without metallic gratings. The three different devices can response to different wavebands. According to the Fourier spectrum result, the peak wavelengths of the three devices are 15.86, 18.92 and 26 μm, respectively. Our work successfully realizes the modulation of photoelectric response wavelength and provides a novel THz detector for the application of national security, astronomical observation and life sciences.

articleTitle: Secure Bar Code Reader for the THz Region
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We Designed a new bar code reader based on leaky parallel plate waveguide. The barcode can be produced easily and can be used securely compared to optical bar codes.

articleTitle: Determining the Magnetic Configuration of Crystalline Solids with Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Magnetic materials are increasingly garnering attention for modern technological applications because of their magnetoelectric properties, which can be modified by external magnetic fields, temperature, and pressure. To utilize magnetic solids in advanced applications, accurate descriptions and details about temperature-dependent spin ordering (antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases) within the magnetic materials must be understood with atomic-level precision. Low-frequency vibrational dynamics can be used to investigate ground state structure-property relationship of magnetic structures, as demonstrated here for FePO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>.

articleTitle: Design of W-band Relativistic Surface-Wave Oscillator with Sheet Electron Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Relativistic surface-wave oscillator driven by 600 kV, 1 kA sheet electron beam is designed and preliminary experiments were carried out. 2-D simulations based both on quasi-optical theory and on the PIC code predict that the device can operate at the π-mode of the rectangular grating providing the output power of up to 70-100 MW at the frequency of 75 GHz. In the initial experiments, a thin sheet electron beam was injected from a blade-shaped explosive cathode and guided very close to the rectangular corrugation resulting the 80-GHz radiation pulses with 3 ns duration.

articleTitle: Generation of Terahertz Transients from Co2Fe0.4Mn0.6Si Heusler alloy/Heavy-Metal Bilayers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We generated electro magnetic transients with a frequency content up to the terahertz regime from Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Si Heusler alloy/heavy-metal bilayers by excitation with fs-laser pulses. We ascribe the generation process to the inverse spin Hall effect. We compared our results with ferromagnetic resonance measurements to investigate the efficiency of interfacial spin currents. We observed that the efficiency of the THz radiation can be described by the spin-orbit coupling, nonetheless the interface properties play an important role.

articleTitle: Achiral Metasurfaces-Induced Circular Polarization Differential Transmittance
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Chiral metasurfaces have different interactions with circularly polarized incidences, showing as circular dichroism and optical activity. Here, we adopt achiral meta-atoms to achieve the function similar to chirality by spin decoupling. Specifically, for two circularly polarized illuminations, one channel is scattering randomly, and the other channel transmits directly or is designed for realizing a specific function. The proposed scheme shows greater flexibility than previous schemes which require elaborate designed structure of the meta-atoms to achieve chirality.

articleTitle: FM to AM Transition of RF Driven THz QCL Comb States
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quantum Cascade Lasers are powerful frequency comb sources in the THz and their repetition rate can be stabilized by means of RF injection locking. By exceeding certain RF injection powers, the spectral shape can be changed significantly with often unidentified effect on the temporal intensity profile. Here we perform temporal intensity profile measurements by means of Shifted Wave Interference Fourier Transform Spectroscopy by employing a fast, antenna coupled superconducting NbN Hot Electron Bolometer. We investigate the intensity profile of strong RF injected heterogeneous THz QCLs showing a strongly AM emission. Additionally, we measure fundamental as well as harmonic comb states under reduced RF injection which exhibit a FM emission.

articleTitle: Enhanced High Harmonic and Terahertz Generation from LiNbO3 Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces exhibit high damage thresholds and strong enhancement of the driving field, making them attractive platforms to control the high-field processes at the nanoscale. Here we report enhanced non-perturbative high-harmonic and terahertz emission from a LiNbO3 metasurface. The harmonic and terahertz intensity are enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to unpatterned samples. The enhanced high harmonics and terahertz waves are highly anisotropic with respect to the excitation polarization and are selective by the excitation wavelength due to its resonant features.

articleTitle: Terahertz Spectroscopic Measurement of the Intraocular Pressure and Diagnosis of the Corneal Endothelial Layer Damage
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A THz-TDS corneal 3D scanner was designed and used to investigate tissue water content perturbations caused by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP). We show that the correlation between increased THz amplitude in the 0.3 and 0.6 THz and IOP levels can be used for non-contact measurement of the IOP. The SEM images confirmed degrees of damage to the endothelial layer.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional terahertz imaging using an amplitude-modulated resonant-tunneling-diode oscillator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on a three-dimensional imaging system obtained by combining an amplitude-modulated continuous-wave (AMCW) radar with two-dimensional mechanical scanning. The system is based on a resonant-tunneling-diode (RTD) oscillator emitting at 660 GHz and modulated at 4.5 GHz. The axial distance measurement relies on determining the phase of the demodulated signal by means of an IQ mixer. With careful calibration, the distance measurement error was reduced to 20 µm.

articleTitle: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated circuits for terahertz generation and detection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We introduce an electro-optic interface from low-loss thin-film lithium niobate for on-chip THz emission and detection. The technology has the ability to custom-tailor the in-device properties to generate terahertz (THz) radiation on-demand by optical rectification in on-chip waveguides, as well as to reach the standard quantum limit of electrical field detection.

articleTitle: Novel High Transmittance Terahertz Microfluidic Chip and Terahertz Spectrum Analysis of Different Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a double-layer terahertz microfluidic chip is fabricated using a cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) material with high transmittance to terahertz waves, and combined with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy to study 5 kinds of sodium salt the terahertz spectrum characteristics of the solution. The results show that the terahertz spectral intensity characteristics of electrolyte solutions composed of different anions and the same cation are different, so that the spectral characteristics of other electrolyte solutions can be inferred from the spectral information of these detected ions.

articleTitle: Super-radiation Terahertz Source Based On Sub-picosecond Electron Beam At CTFEL
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: China Academy of Engineering Physics Terahertz Free Electron Laser (CTFEL) works in the range of 0.7~4.2 THz. To expand the range below 0.1 THz, we developed a super-radiation terahertz (THz) source based on sub-picosecond electron beam behind CTFEL. The sub-picosecond electron beam was generated by velocity compression and then injected into undulator to provide THz wave. In this proceeding, the preliminary experimental results of super-radiation terahertz source were reported.

articleTitle: Polyimide as Antenna Substrate for THz InP-Based Resonant Tunnelling Diode Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a patch antenna fabricated on a thin Polyimide (PI) substrate (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=3.5) is proposed. The antenna can be fabricated for same chip integration with the promising indium phosphide (InP) based resonant tunneling diode (RTD) terahertz (THz) oscillator. The proposed antenna is isolated from the InP by the ground plane which is placed between the InP and PI materials. The proposed structure can solve the antenna performance issues caused by the thick and large dielectric constant InP substrate (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=12.54) when used as antenna substrate. The antenna is designed at 300 GHz. The simulated results show air-side radiation and the effects of the InP on the antenna performance is eliminated.

articleTitle: Investigation of quasi-bound states in the continuum in terahertz metal complementary periodic cross-shaped resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We numerically and experimentally demonstrate quasi-bound states in the continuum (BICs) in the free-standing metal complementary periodic cross-shaped resonators (CPCRs). Such induced quasi-BICs arise from the broken symmetry in CPCRs. By slightly breaking mirror symmetry through reducing the length of one arm in CPCRs, the measured Q factor of the quasi-BICs can reach 102, which is significantly high compared with that of the conventional modes and could even be improved by further reducing the structural asymmetry factor. The sharp quasi-BICs realized in the structure may immediately boost the exploration of ultra-narrowband filters and ultra-sensitive sensors at terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: Detecting aqueous samples by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Due to the strong absorption of Terahertz (THz) waves by water, the development of THz detection technology in biomedical field is seriously restricted. In this paper, a convenient and promising method for the detection of THz spectra of hydrated substances is proposed. The detection of α-lactose solution was demonstrated, the spectral range is from 0.1 to 1.5 THz and the sensitivity can reach the order of femtomole.

articleTitle: Application of Titanium-based Microbolometers in Terahertz Time-Domain Spectrometers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Titanium-based antenna coupled microbolometers (Ti-μbolometers) were applied for a spatial mode control of terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) systems. The response spectra of Ti-μbolometers with three different antenna designs – narrow-band dipole antenna for 0.3 THz, 0.7 THz and a log-periodic antenna for a wide-band detection – were investigated. The spatial profiles of focused and unfocused beams were recorded. It was shown that the Ti-μbolometers can serve as useful instruments in optical alignment and monitoring of spatial mode features in THz-TDS system.

articleTitle: Metamaterial integrated circular polarization quantum well infrared photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A metamaterial integrated circular polarization long-wavelength quantum well infrared photodetector is presented. A maximum circular polarization extinction ratio of 4.2:1 is achieved at 1037.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> (9.64 μm), which is more than two times higher than previously reported values. The metamaterial also enhances the responsivity by one order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable physical unclonable functions in infrared wavebands base on VO2 phase transition nanomaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Optical physical unclonable function (PUF) is one of the most promising hardware security solutions which have been proven to be hardened against machine learning attack. However, the disordered structures of traditional optical PUFs are usually determined after manufacturing. Here, VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> phase transition nanomaterials are proposed to construct reconfigurable PUFs in infrared, giving a promising way to enlarge the key space and code capacity of optical PUF.

articleTitle: Distinctive millimeter-wave band electromagnetic properties of µm-thick Al-Si films upon dielectric substrates
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Results of experimental study of the reflection and transmission losses in the V-band of µm-thick Si-Al films on the dielectric substrates are considered. Two sources magnetron co-sputtering deposition of Si-Al alloys was utilized to prepare a series of coatings of varied chemical composition and thus different properties. Control over films composition was provided by variation of Al magnetron power source with constant Si magnetron power source. Segregation of Si and Al atoms in Al-Si films was observed at a specific power of Al magnetron source during the deposition: Si atoms were mainly concentrated at the lower levels of the film adjacent to the substrate, while Al atoms tended to concentrate near the upper surface of the coating. Distinct electromagnetic properties of Al-Si films fabricated at the transient phase of segregation mode were observed: one side of the film demonstrated low reflection in the millimeter-band while almost full reflection was observed from the other side. Such properties of µm-thick Si-Al films upon dielectric substrates can be useful for development of millimeter-wave antenna modules technology.

articleTitle: Tip-enhanced infrared nanospectroscopy of microvesiscles
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present infrared (IR) nanospectroscopy results obtained on single hundred-nanometer-sized lipid microvesicles. The use of an IR nanospectroscopy platform allowed us to identify heterogeneities of the molecular cargo of the microvesicles that would not be possible by conventional IR spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Phaseless Terahertz Coded-Aperture Imaging Based on Deep Phase Compensation Gradient Descent Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we propose a phaseless terahertz coded-aperture imaging (PL-TCAI) method, which is able to achieve high-resolution reconstruction of the target at low intensity measurements and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by utilizing the compensating phase information and deep generative model. Simulation experiments show that the proposed method has a competitive imaging performance compared with the state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: THz Spectroscopy of the Anisotropic Refractive Index of β-Ga2O3
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated the monoclinic β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor using transmission terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). To characterize the anisotropic properties, the complex refractive index of a semi-insulating bulk and of an n-type Si-doped homoepitaxial film were obtained along the [100] and [010] directions. The material response can be well-described by the Drude-Lorentz model, from which the static permittivity and the electrical properties were determined in good agreement with electrical contact measurements.

articleTitle: Effect of the Gate Length on Terahertz Heterodyne detection Based on GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, room-temperature terahertz heterodyne mixers based on GaN high-electron-mobility transistors are studied. For comparison, asymmetric antennas with gate lengths of L=170 nm and L=600 nm are specially designed to couple with terahertz waves ranging from 320-345 GHz, respectively. It is found that the performance of mixer for L=170 nm, such as the optical sensitivity and the conversion loss, is obviously superior to the one for L=600 nm.

articleTitle: Comparison of five precision assembly methods for terahertz TWT electron gun’s cathode and gate electrode
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presented a multiple directions precision adjustment device, which was used for adjusting the coaxially of the travelling wave tube (TWT) electron gun’s cathode and gate electrode. The concentricity can meet the requirements only by rotating the three micrometer calipers. It can be quickly adjusted to 0.01 mm in 15 mins. The results are helpful to the following terahertz TWT, using a 17 kV, 71 mA electron beam, the measured peak power is over 60 watt and the average output power is over 12 watts with 20% duty cycle at the frequency around 0.22 THz.

articleTitle: Sensitivity characterization of a photomultiplier tube for terahertz radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we present the first sensitivity characterization of a photomultiplier tube (PMT) for the detection of terahertz (THz) radiation. The PMT holds a metasurface-based photocathode that emits electrons via the electron field emission effect. This leads to a very non-linear detector that allows one to see much smaller variations of an incident signal than the absolute signal strength itself. We find that this particular PMT has a detection threshold for a THz pulse of 1 nJ and a detection confidence level of 99.7% within 55 – 250 pJ, depending on the THz pulse energy.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of Dielectric-Loaded Waveguide Circuits for Gyro-TWTs Based on An Automatic Root-Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, an automatic root-search (ARS) algorithm is proposed to design the dielectric-loaded gyro-TWT with specified goal. It costs less computation sources in comparison with the 3D simulation and can recognize the eigenmode automatically. The 220 GHz dielectric-loaded gyro-TWT has been examined based on the ARS algorithm. As an example, the maximum circuit loss of 59 dB/cm for ${\text{HE}}_{12}^{\text{d}}$ mode is achieved at the backward-wave oscillation frequency, corresponding to the dielectric property of tanδ=0.35, ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=5 and a thickness of 0.3mm.

articleTitle: High-Power Microwave Oscillation of a 94 GHz Gyrotron for Air-Breakdown Plasma Observations in Microwave Rocket
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report high-power microwave oscillation of a 94 GHz gyrotron, contributing to the study on air breakdown plasma in Microwave Rocket. The gyrotron is demountable, adopting a diode magnetron injection gun and a built-in quasi-optical mode converter, installed in a compact superconducting magnet with a bore diameter of 100 mm. In this study, microwave signal was detected using a pyroelectric detector and a liquid thermograph sheet at the beam voltage of 40 kV and beam current of about 20 A. Besides, air breakdown plasma, useful for the thrust generation of Microwave Rocket, was successfully ignited at atmospheric pressure. The observed plasma's filamentary structure at the propagation velocity of 720 m/s was different from 170 GHz, which indicates a frequency dependence of the plasma structure.

articleTitle: High-Q Fano resonance induced by Rayleigh anomaly in terahertz metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: High-Q Fano resonance is excited from the hybridization of eigenmode and Rayleigh anomaly through introducing the tiny displacements in the designed terahertz metamaterial. The strength of Fano resonance can be controlled via varying the incident angle of terahertz waves. These results provide new insights into the design of terahertz devices.

articleTitle: Cavity based high resolution THz spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A high finesse cavity operating around 620 GHz has been constructed to improve the sensitivity limit for the measurement of weakly absorbing gases. An effective path length of 1 km is achieved significantly improving the available sensitivity. The measurement of the cavity decay time allows the quantification of the absorption coefficient.

articleTitle: Simulated Verification for a Finite Rate of Innovation Method Applied to Terahertz Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Methods utilizing finite rate of innovation theory have been employed to achieve low sampling rates in ultrasound experiments. Here, we apply this theory to create a terahertz specific method to gain the benefits of faster signal processing speeds and data acquisition compared with current standard processing methods. We verify our method by simulating a THz like signal, adding Gaussian noise, using a low sampling rate, processing it through our code and then comparing the reconstructed output to the original simulated signal to find close agreement.

articleTitle: A Parallel Decision Feedback Equalizer Structure For Terahertz High-speed Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to propose a new structure for LMS equalization using parallel decision feedback equalizer (DFE) to achieving 20Gbps communication capacity. The structure is implemented on the Xilinx XCKU115-FLVD1924 FPGA chip. In order to achieve 20Gbps capacity, 16QAM signal and 156.25MHz clock frequency is applied. This scheme contributes a new parallel signal processing realization for high speed wireless signal processing in FPGA.

articleTitle: First Generation of Vortex Plasmons via Vortex-Beam End-Fire Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) carrying an orbital angular momentum were first obtained at a cylindrical brass-ZnS-air interface due to the diffraction of perfect vortex beams at the front end of a cylinder. The beams with a wavelength of 141 µm resulted from the transformation of a Gaussian beam of a free electron laser using a binary axicon and a lens. The propagation of rotating plasmons along an axisymmetric surface over a distance of 70 mm and their diffraction at the rear end of a cylindrical transmission line with conservation of the topological charge of the diffracted free wave were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Key Problems of Terahertz Frequency Conversion Technology (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper summarizes some key problems of terahertz frequency conversion technology based on Schottky diode, including device manufacturing, device modeling and circuit design technology and introduces our recent advances in these aspects. In particular, two novel diode structures, such as double-barrier structure and multi-finger structure, will be presented. Besides, modeling process based on physical symbolic defined device (SDD) for the intrinsic part of diode will be described in detail. Finally, general circuit design techniques for terahertz frequency conversion circuits are summarized.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of a Transmission-Type Waveguide Power Equalizer for a Ka-Band Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a transmission-type power equalizer based on metallic rectangular waveguide with good tunability, high power handling capacity and simple structure for a Ka-band gyrotron travelling wave tube (gyro-TWT) is proposed. To verify the feasibility of the equalizer, a prototype operated at 32-35.5 GHz is fabricated and measured. The vector network analyzer (VNA) measurement results were in good agreement with the CST simulations.

articleTitle: Modeling the THz response of antenna-coupled Silicon MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The validation of simulations tools for microelectronic devices and circuits at frequencies reaching high into the THz regime is a challenging task. For the case of Si MOSFETs used as detectors of cw THz radiation, we show that both the TSMC RF foundry model and our physics-based in-house tool ADS-HDM, which is designed to capture plasmonic channel effects at all frequencies correctly, reproduce the performance of detectors from 0.4 to 1.2 THz remarkably well. The good agreement between the two models has its roots in the short momentum scattering time of charge carriers in the channels of MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Sheet Resistance Measurement of Thin Metal Films Using Reflection-Mode THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Micro four-point probe technology can reliably be used to measure the sheet resistance of thin metal films, with great accuracy and repeatability. In this work, we investigate the suitability of using reflection-mode teraherz time-domain spectroscopy for the same task. The agreement between the two methods places reflection-mode terahertz time-domain spectroscopy as a viable tool for thin metal film analysis.

articleTitle: Development of a high signal-to-noise ratio terahertz-wave parametric generator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this study, noise-free THz-wave output from an injection-seeded THz-wave parametric generator (is-TPG) was achieved by high-power injection seeding. The THz signal and broadband noise originated from different positions in the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystal, and only the pure THz signal was successfully extracted. Using this system, quantitative spectroscopy of high attenuation reagents (above −60 dB) was successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Sub-Terahertz Vortex Beam Generator Using Spiral Metal Reflector
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Vortex beam is a ring-shaped beam that possesses a sub-wavelength null point in the center formed by angular phase variation. It is useful for a wide range of applications including imaging, wireless communications, and photophoretic trapping. In this study, we propose a reflector-type millimeter-wave vortex beam generator using a spiral metal structure designed for the WR10 band (75-110 GHz). We mapped out its radiation pattern by translating a Schottky barrier diode, and we confirmed the formation of a ring-shaped beam at the WR 10 band. Furthermore, we also confirmed that the proposed device can generate both of the orthogonal polarizations, which is distinctive from the conventional approaches based on holographic diffraction gratings.

articleTitle: Quantitative determination of the density of photo-excited charge carriers by s-SNOM with field-effect-transistor-based THz detection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We show that the phase information of coherent scattering-type Scanning Near-Field Optical Microscopy allows to quantitatively determine the charge carrier concentration of semiconductors. This is demonstrated with measurements at 257.6 GHz on photoexcited charge carriers in Si. The measurement system employs for the first time a TeraFET detector (an antenna-equipped field-effect transistor), in this case fabricated in Si CMOS technology.

articleTitle: TE02 – TE01 waveguide mode converter designed based on particle swarm algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the contour parameters of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> – TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> waveguide mode converter to improve the efficiency of the mode converter. A 220GHz TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> – TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> waveguide mode converter is designed, with a conversion efficiency of 99.23%, a bandwidth of 7.7%, and a power capacity of 56MW.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation on Permeability Change in Cell Membrane by Terahertz Irradiation-Induced Hydrophilic Pores
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Currently, it is indicated that terahertz irradiation is capable of permeabilizing cell membrane by electroporation, which is able to facilitate transmembrane transport of molecules and ions for medicine and clinical applications. This paper numerically studies the changes in cell membrane permeability to ions owing to membrane hydrophilic pores by electroporation in response to terahertz picosecond pulse train. The capacitive current and ion channel currents of cell membrane are taken into account in the simulation of membrane conductance of the hydrophilic pores. The numerical simulation results reveal that the membrane permeability to ions by terahertz irradiation increases firstly at the locations around the two poles of a cell where the membrane is nearly perpendicular to the terahertz electric fields. And then the increase in the permeability gradually extends towards the parts of the cell where the cell membrane is nearly parallel to the terahertz electric fields. The results also show that the larger the amplitude of terahertz irradiation is, the earlier the membrane conductance of a whole cell starts to increase and the larger the conductance can be.

articleTitle: A 330GHz Multi-Channel Radar for Interferometric Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a 330GHz multi-channel radar system is introduced, which has single transmitter and four receivers for interferometric inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging. The experimental results verify the high-resolution three-dimensional imaging ability of the system, by which the detailed scattering distribution of the target can be obtained.

articleTitle: Lorentz contraction of an electric field around relativistic electron beams
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spatio-temporal terahertz electric field profiles around 35 MeV electron bunches propagating in the air are measured by the echelon-based single-shot electro-optic measurement with a sub-picosecond temporal resolution. We demonstrates that the Lorentz contraction of the electric field in the direction perpendicular to the pass of the electron beams is directly observed.

articleTitle: Metal Dopants Increase THz-Photoconductivity in g-C3N4
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metal-doped graphitic carbon nitride has shown promise in the field of photocatalysis due to its increased efficiency over its pure form. In this work, we show that Cu doping g-C3N4 does not perturb the structure of the materials and extends the visible light absorption. Ultrafast THz-photoconductivity of carbon nitride is enhanced due to the addition of metal dopant. A Cu dopant creates a very fast photoconductivity component (727 fs) in the optical pump terahertz probe (OPTP) trace. We also studied the influence of film preparation which can create a long lifetime (~100 ps) component in the photoconductivity.

articleTitle: A Dual Stub Loaded Compact UWB Antenna Offering Notch Band Feature
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An ultra-wide band (UWB) antenna having a notch band is proposed in this article. The antenna structure comprises of a pentagonal radiator loaded with dual stub. The bottom is utilized to enhance the bandwidth while the upper stub is utilized to achieve notch band. The antenna with compact size of 15 × 20 × 0.254 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> operates over 3.1 – 14.7 GHz along with a notch band of 3.8 – 4.7 GHz providing more than 2.3 dBi gain, while it decreases up to -4 dBi in notched band region. Moreover, the wide bandwidth, compact size, simple geometrical structure, high gain and efficiency makes the proposed work a potential candidate for physically small devices.

articleTitle: Miniature particle-accelerator using THz pulses to drive cascade symmetric dielectric prisms
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The particle accelerators have tremendous application prospects in basic physics, energy science, medicine, and other fields. However, the size and cost of traditional radio frequency accelerators fundamentally limit their popularity and accessibility. To achieve continuous acceleration, we propose and simulate a millimeter-scale particle accelerator using readily available THz pulses to drive three-stage cascade symmetric dielectric prisms. By calculation and simulation, we show that a mean energy gain of 1.057 MeV can be obtained from a 7- millimeter device. The corresponding acceleration gradient is over 300 MV/m, which is quite attractive for the development of on- chip particle accelerators for broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Study on the Mode Switching in the System of Two Delay-Coupled Gyrotron Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz-range gyrotrons operating in a continuous-wave mode are of great interest for many applications, such as spectroscopy, plasma diagnostics, biomedical research, etc. Some of these applications require fast frequency tuning. In this paper, we demonstrate the possibility of fast stepwise frequency tuning by switching between the modes of in-phase and anti-phase synchronization in the system of two coupled gyrotrons.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Vibrational Spectra of Amoxicillin and Ampicillin
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Amoxicillin and ampicillin are large, flexible antibiotic molecules that are commonly administered in their solid trihydrate forms. The hydration of these pharmaceuticals has been studied in this work using both terahertz and low-frequency Raman vibrational spectroscopies to measure the vibrational modes of the crystalline solids below 200 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Combining the experimental results with solid-state density functional theory simulations of both structure and vibrations, allows for the in-depth exploration of the potential energy surfaces governing the large-amplitude motions of the co-crystalized waters.

articleTitle: Two beam self mixing interference in terahertz quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The THz quantum cascade laser (THz-QCL) based two-beam self mixing (SM) interference is achieved by re-injecting optical feedbacks from two independent targets into the laser cavity. The two-beam SM effect manifests itself in the variation of laser terminal voltage. Information of the relative position change of the two targets can be obtained by analyzing the amplitude and phase of the SM signal. Using this method, micron-scale thickness variation of a GaAs sample, about one percent of the laser wavelength, is accurately measured. Our study provides an available way to develop new terahertz nondestructive testing technology.

articleTitle: Electron-optical System for a Q-band Helix Traveling-wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, an electron-optical system for a Q-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) is proposed to meet the demand of future wireless communications. Based on the electron beam parameters required for the Q-band TWT, a dual-anode electron gun and periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing configuration are designed. The CST simulation results show that the beam voltage, current and waist radius of the pencil electron beam are 8.7 kV, 70 mA, and 0.135 mm, respectively. The electron beam can transport through the helix slow-wave structure with a length of more than 100 mm and the static beam transmission can reach over 99.8% in CST simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a 57-64GHz Sub-Harmonic Mixer With Planar Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 57-64GHz planar sub-harmonic mixer based on anti-parallel GaAs Schottky diodes is proposed in this paper. Planar microstrip circuit is used with flip Schottky diodes mounted on top of it, making the circuit very easy to fabricate and assemble. Co-simulation of three-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation software HFSS and circuit simulation software ADS are adopted to optimize the performance. Accurate modeling of planar Schottky diode is implemented, and then matching circuits of the mixer are designed and optimized. The simulation results show that the conversion loss of the harmonic mixer is less than 7 dB at 57-64GHz with LO power of 6.2~12.5dBm at 26GHz. The lowest conversion loss of 6.2dB is achieved with LO power of 11.2dBm.

articleTitle: Terahertz Sensors for non-Destructive Primer Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quality control of primer layers in safety-relevant bonded joints is essential for the long-term stability of the such components. For this purpose, Terahertz time-domain imaging in reflection geometry is being used as a technology to inspect the multilayered structure and determine the thicknesses of the different layers with high resolution by applying sparse deconvolution.

articleTitle: Actively modulated broadband Terahertz Absorbers realized by VOx thin films
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz stealth and shielding devices with low reflection and strong absorption are promising in terahertz (THz) communication and radar. In this study, active THz reflection and absorption properties based on strong correlated electron oxides VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> (x= 1.5, 2) thin films are investigated. By varying the laser fluence, the reflection can be modulated to near 0 and the absorption can be tuned to near 70%. Our work suggest strong correlated electron oxide films could provide a possible approach for the design of tunable THz stealth and shielding devices.

articleTitle: Simulation study of D-band extended interaction klystron amplifier
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A D-band extended interaction klystron amplifier is investigated. A traveling wave structure is adopted as the input and output structure to improve the bandwidth. When the operating voltage is 22 kV, and current is 0.3 A. The simulation results show that a maximum output power of 450 W is obtained with the input power of 31.25 mW, the corresponding gain is 41.5 dB, efficiency is 6.8%, and a 3-dB bandwidth of about 600 MHz can be achieved. Our work provides a feasible method to the improvement of bandwidth for the extended interaction klystron amplifier.

articleTitle: Terahertz emission from HgTe nanocrystals excited by femtosecond optical pulses
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Large HgTe nanocrystals are very attractive for THz technology since they possess strong intraband absorption at THz frequencies with hot carrier relaxation times of few picoseconds. Here, we demonstrate that large HgTe nanocrystals excited by femtosecond optical pulses emit coherent THz emission from 0.2 THz to 2.5 THz. Our study reveals the great potential of HgTe nanocrystals as an original scheme for coherent THz emission.

articleTitle: An Nb5N6 microbolometer THz camera
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This article mainly introduces our research group’s latest progress in THz camera. Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> film is a THz sensitive material and has a significant prospect in THz detection. We use this material to fabricate an antenna coupled microbolometer THz detector array at room temperature, and integrated 180 nm CMOS process readout circuit. The THz camera has a resolution of 32×32, pixel size of 250×250 μm, frame rate of 30, working range is 0.25-1 THz. Compared with the type of pyro-electric infrared camera, below 1 THz terahertz spectrum has significant advantages, with a higher response rate and a lower NEP.

articleTitle: Study of Generation and Detection of Continuous Terahertz Wave Using Chaotic Multi-mode Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 650-nm chaotically oscillating multi-mode semiconductor laser was used to generate and detect a stable continuous terahertz signal from a photoconductive antenna. The intensity of the generated terahertz was ~10 times stronger compared to the excitation without chaotic oscillations. The frequency comb-type spectrum is obtained in the sub-terahertz region, which makes terahertz time-domain spectroscopy systems with this kind of economically superior laser very promising for the evaluation of 5G and 6G components.

articleTitle: A Cryogenic Readout Integrated Circuit Designed For the Blocked-Impurity-Band Terahertz Detector
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This article proposes a cryogenic readout integrated circuit (ROIC) for the blocked-impurity-band (BIB) Terahertz detector. The cryogenic ROIC is composed of a capacitance transimpedance amplifier (CTIA) input-stage circuit, a correlated double sampling (CDS) circuit and an output-stage circuit. The circuit design is based on a cryogenic MOSFET model obtained by optimizing some parameters of BSIM4 according to previous cryogenic test results. The ROIC and BIB detector are interconnected by wire bonding, and the output characteristics are measured at 6K. Our result shows that the circuit has realized the design function under cryogenic conditions.

articleTitle: 220GHz High Bit Rate Inter-Satellite Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 220GHz communication system is designed and manufactured.For applications in space-distributed satellite networks, 5Gbps code rate level 100m communication is realized between satellites under THz carrier frequency.The system carrier frequency covers 210GHz to 230GHz. The baseband signal at the transmitter side is modulated directly on the carrier, multiplied and then mixed with the modulated signal before transmitting. At the receiving end, the signal is received by the antenna and output by the duplexer to a LNA, then down-converted to the IF unit after frequency doubling and harmonic mixer, and demodulated at IF to output the I/Q baseband signal to the signal processing unit.

articleTitle: Recent Research for G-band CW transformed folded waveguide TWT
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Institute of Applied Electronics has developed a wideband continuous waves (CW) transformed folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (TFWTWT) amplifier operating at G-band. By the measurement, the amplifier produced the maximum output power 28.27W in frequency 220GHz with 7GHz -3dB bandwidth at CW work. The maximum gain is 31.4dB in frequency 221GHz.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Metasurfaces Based on Carbon Nanotube Film for THz Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present carbon nanotube films metamaterials exhibiting extraordinary transmission at the resonant peaks in the THz wave region. Experiment and theory reveal that the transmission resonant peaks originated from the surface plasmon polaritons resonance, which can be changed through altering the lattice constant of array. The proposed metasurfaces were demonstrated to be efficient in THz sensor for pesticides concentrate.

articleTitle: Generation of Ka-Band Superradiant Pulses for High-Gradient Acceleration of Electrons in a Scheme with Two Coaxial Beams
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter-range generators of uniquely short (sub-nanosecond) GW-level Cherenkov superradiant (SR) pulses looks promising for high-gradient acceleration of electrons in non-superconducting metallic structures without the development of breakdown phenomena. In this paper, we propose the high-gradient acceleration scheme with two coaxial electron beams one of which (internal) is accelerated in a pillbox structure by a 250 ps/0.5 GW Ka-band SR pulse generated by the external beam due to interaction with the backward wave in periodical slow-wave structure. According to PIC simulations with parameters of the planning experiment, the accelerating gradient (rate of energy gain) in such a scheme can reach 350-400 MeV/m, which significantly exceeds characteristics of modern accelerators based on X-band klystrons.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopy of liquid crystals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: FTIR technique was employed to study two liquid crystals of the BA class. The THz transmission spectra of the two compounds are characterized by distinct absorption bands. 4-hexylbenzoic acid is characterized by 7 absorption bands while 4-octyloxybenzoic acid has 11 absorption bands. Despite the similarities in the molecular structures of these compounds, there are profound differences in their spectra.

articleTitle: Phase diagram method for efficient THz images reconstructing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In order to increase THz images quality, we show that the effect of multiplicative perturbation can be notably removed by using the concept of phase diagram associated with a Frenet-Serret-based quantification.

articleTitle: Lens based Focal Plane Arrays Coupled to Distributed Absorbers: Imaging System Trade-offs
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: To characterize the spectral coupling between a lens based Focal Plane Array and its Quasi-Optical system, Coherent Fourier Optics methodology is employed. A lens absorber design is proposed and compared to an existing bare absorber-based imaging system. It is shown that the performance of the two imagers is comparable in terms of aperture efficiency, Point Spread Function, and normalized throughput. Moreover, the proposed lens absorber achieves 5 folds better NETD in comparison to the bare absorber due to its smaller physical area. A prototype of the proposed geometry is under fabrication as a proof of concept.

articleTitle: Stability of optical beats in laser chaos for THz wave generation and detection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Stability of optical beats between longitudinal laser modes in a chaotically oscillated laser diodes for THz wave generation and detection is demonstrated compared to a free-running continuous-wave laser conventional laser. The high stability of chaotically oscillating lasers makes these lasers promising candidates for optical pump sources in terahertz time-domain spectroscopy systems.

articleTitle: Experimental research of 45GHz quasi-optical transmission line for deep drilling
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The 45GHz quasi-optical transmission line for deep drilling has been designed, machined and experimental tested in this paper. Based on the Stratton-Chu formula and mirror optimization program, the structure of the three quasi-optical mirrors which transmit the wave beam from the Gyrotron to rock surface has been obtained. The output power of the Gyrotron is adjustable from 0kW to 20kW. The experiment results show that the output power density meets the preliminary requirements to melt the rock. The maximum temperature of the sample stone reached to 2032.6°C.

articleTitle: Synthesis Method for Highly Oversized Serpentine Mode Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this article, the method to design highly oversized circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> serpentine mode converter is proposed. The mode coupling in oversized elliptical waveguides is firstly analyzed, and their ability to suppressing the generation of parasitic modes is illustrated. For a high conversion efficiency and broad bandwidth, elliptical waveguides are introduced into the mode converters as the transmission structure. In order to validate the analysis, a highly oversized mode converter working in W band is designed and simulated. Results indicate that a relative bandwidth more than 20% with a conversion efficiency over 95% is achieved under the conversion length of 1.15 m.

articleTitle: On the possibility of unipolar terahertz pulses generation in nonequilibrium plasma formed by the ultrashort UV laser pulse
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We perform the new approach to produce highly unipolar terahertz pulses. The idea is based on the nonuniform amplification of seed ultrashort one-cycle CEP pulses in nonequilibrium fast relaxing plasma of air or nitrogen. If the gain coefficient drops significantly within the duration of one-cycle CEP pulse, it undergoes significant distortion where the leading edge of the pulse is amplified and the trailing tail of opposite polarity is absorbed. The obtained results involve self-consistent solution of second-order wave equation and kinetic Boltzmann equation for the electron velocity distribution function relaxation.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of Plasmon-Polaritons in Plasmonic THz Detector Integrated with Two-Dimensional Nano-Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Plasmon-polariton modes in an InGaAs-HEMT-based plasmonic THz detector integrated with 2D nano-antennas are theoretically investigated. We show that the incident THz wave polarized in the channel width direction can be converted into a cross-polarized plasmon mode in the channel length direction via the 2D nano-antennas, indicating a possibility of realizing polarization-insensitive THz detection by the plasmonic detector.

articleTitle: Study of the mode converter for terahertz band vacuum tube
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a mode converter from rectangular waveguide TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> to TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf> Mode at Terahertz band is proposed. Firstly, a square-circle transition is used to convert the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode in the rectangular waveguide into the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in the circular waveguide. Secondly, based on the coupled wave theory, the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode is converted into HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode through smooth wall circular waveguide. Finally, in terms of the Stratton-Chu formula and mirror optimization program, the structure of the two quasi-optical mirrors which transmit the wave beam to the window successfully has been obtained. The simulation results show that the power transmission efficiency of the designed TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>-TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf> mode converter from the input of the rectangular waveguide to the vacuum window is 96.1% at a center frequency of 1030 GHz. The designed mode converter has a simple structure and easy to machine.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metamaterials with InGaZnO Schottky Barrier Diodes at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: we propose electrically reconfigurable metamaterials (MTMs) at terahertz (THz) frequencies using InGaZnO (IGZO) Schottky barrier diodes, achieving a continuous amplitude modulation of 13%. The IGZO film was deposited at the capacitive gap of electric-field-coupled inductor-capacitor (ELC) MTMs. By sweeping the depletion region with DC bias, the averaged conductivity of IGZO film is changed, and thus the reconfiguration is accomplished. Upon varying the film conductivity, the simulated transmission can be modulated from 14.5 to -9.9 dB at 0.39 THz, corresponding to a modulation depth of 13%. Such active metamaterials address many attractive advantages, including not only low cost and simple fabrication process but also reasonable modulation depth and large area for several inch-scale.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Undulator Radiation from Short Electron Bunches into the Dominant Mode of an Oversized Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A possibility to generate wideband terahertz pulses of Coherent Spontaneous Radiation with energies of hundreds of microjoules and a relatively high efficiency in regimes close to group synchronism of electrons with the mode of a circular waveguide has been demonstrated in simulations. As a magnetic system of the THz source providing a large undulator parameter K> 1, it is proposed to use the simplest helical undulator formed by several permanently magnetized ferromagnetic helices. The use of a preliminary energetic chirp of particles and stabilization of the bunch in the field of the emitted electromagnetic pulse makes it possible to mitigate the effects of Coulomb repulsion of particles and to increase the length of the effective interaction of a dense bunch with the field of the operating mode.

articleTitle: High Absorption of Goldblack Film for a pyroelectric detector based on ultra-thin LiTaO3 crystal
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This letter reports on the performance of LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> based pyroelectric single-element detectors coated with a nanos-tructured thin-film absorber consisting of the NiCr material as the sensor electrodes. Goldblack film have been proven to be an effective absorption layer for pyroelectric detectors. Improving the absorption can be achieved by adjusting the surface characteristics of goldblack film. Goldblack coatings are low-density amorphous deposits of gold that appear black in the visible and infrared regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. They have absorption close to unity for radiation in this range. Because of the delicate nature of the coatings, they are easily crushed or displaced by touch or even blasts of air, their use has not been extensively exploited but rather the process is re-invented every time a specific requirement appears. This is typified by our requirement to coat a small pixel pyroelectric detector.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Measurements of Broadband Terahertz Properties of Crystals along Two Axes
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We suggest a method to simultaneously measure terahertz optical properties of crystals along two axes in terahertz time-domain spectroscopy using two broadband polarizers. We demonstrate the method by measuring temperature dependence of refractive index and absorption coefficient of lithium triborate crystal along different optical axes.

articleTitle: Wideband Refractive Index Extraction of Low-loss Materials with the Combined TDS-FTIR Method
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A method to obtain the optical constants of low loss materials in a wide frequency range was proposed based on the measured transmission data from THz-TDS and FTIR. With anchoring phase points from TDS, the phase spectrum lost in FTIR original data was successfully retrieved and the complex refractive index was acquired with standard iterative method (Nelder-Mead and Newton-Raphson). As an example, the refractive index and extinction coefficient of HRSi were extracted from 0.5 to 10 THz with both iterative method and analytic formula. Good agreement between TDS and FTIR results in the overlapped frequency range was realized.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation on Injection Locking of the EU 170 GHz 2 MW TE34,19-Mode Coaxial-Cavity Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Injection locking of gyrotron oscillators offers an improved mode stability and the precise phase and frequency control of the generated millimeter-wave signal. It might offer completely new possibilities for applications related to nuclear fusion plasma, spectroscopy, and radar. In this presentation it is shown that the theory of Kurokawa can be applied to understand the injection locking of gyrotrons and that it provides accurate prediction of the locking behavior. Based on that, the investigation on injection locking of the EU 170 GHz 2 MW TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34,19</inf>-mode coaxial-cavity gyrotron using self-consistent single and multimode simulations is presented. Detailed studies on injection signals containing competing modes to account either for signal impurities or for deliberate injection of competing modes are presented.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Frequency-Domain Terahertz Spectroscopy and its Application to Electron Paramagnetic Resonance
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Frequency-domain terahertz (THz) spectroscopy using a continuously tunable photomixer is a powerful analytical technique, offering unique advantages such as high frequency resolution. Here, we report an improved method to increase the spectral resolution using a pair of fiber stretchers. In this method, the amplitude of transmitted THz waves was determined at each frequency by modulating the optical path difference. As a result, the spectral resolution of about 1 MHz was achieved in this study. We applied this technique to frequency-domain electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and successfully observed EPR spectra with a 20-MHz line width.

articleTitle: Controlling directivity pattern and intensity of THz radiation during its generation in a gas-clatter jet
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A supersonic jet consisting of noble gas clusters is considered as a source of terahertz (THz) radiation pumped by high-power femtosecond laser system. We present the results of experimental studies on optimizing the intensity and diagram pattern of the THz radiation generated in cluster jet and demonstrate that under certain conditions of the jet excitation, it is possible to form a cluster filament that radiates THz waves with a maximum intensity along the direction of the laser beam propagation. Provided phenomenological model is in a good agreement with experimental results and well explains observed phenomenon.

articleTitle: Graphene-based thin-films for flexible applications inspected by high-resolution Terahertz near-field inspection
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) inspection is among the most versatile tools to perform non-destructive, quantitative characterization of conductive thin-films. In this work we apply high-resolution THz near-field measurements for the inspection of graphene-based thin-films for flexible applications. We show and discuss sheet resistance results for wafer-scale CVD-grown graphene as well as for conductive thin-films produced from dispersions of exfoliated graphene-flakes on various substrates.

articleTitle: Generation of 150 MW/0.7 ns W-Band Superradiant Pulses in a Strongly Oversized 2D Periodical Surface-Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the results of experiments on generation of sub-nanosecond 90-GHz superradiant (SR) pulses with a record peak power of ~150 MW. Such pulses are produced based on excitation of a surface wave in an oversized waveguide with 2D (double-periodical) corrugation. In such a structure, azimuthally propagating wave fluxes synchronize radiation from different azimuthal segments of a tubular electron bunch with a diameter greatly exceeding the wavelength. The implemented approach opens up the prospect of a radical increase in the total electron current and the peak power of SR pulses while maintaining azimuthal coherence of radiation. The results of experiments are in line with the theoretical predictions within the frame of the quasi-optical model and direct PIC simulations.

articleTitle: The Design of Asymmetrical Planar Terahertz Toroidal Dipole Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We proposed and fabricated J-shaped planar structure metasurfaces to achieve excitation of dual-frequency toroidal dipole resonances. The mutual coupling of two asymmetric J-shaped metal rings lead to two toroidal dipole resonances. The mechanism was revealed by the analysis of the electromagnetic field distribution and the numerical calculation of the multipole moment. The simple and flexible planar toroidal dipole metasurfaces provide more possibilities for the development and application of terahertz functional devices.

articleTitle: Terahertz circular Airy beams carrying power-exponent-phase vortices
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We numerically generate the terahertz circular Airy beams(THz-CABs) with the power-exponent-phase(PEP) vertices. We demonstrate the combination of the PEP vertices and THz-CABs for the extension application of PEP vertices. At the same time, the light path of THz-CABs will be more compact and simpler compared with the optical one.

articleTitle: Application of Higher Harmonics Generation Mode in the Low-Voltage Vacuum Electronic Device with Non-Laminar Electron Beams to Achieve Millimeter-Band Operation
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Application of higher harmonics generation mode in a compact low-voltage vircator-type vacuum electronic device utilizing nonlaminar electron beams operating in millimeter band is considered and preliminary experimental results are reported. Higher harmonics generation was achieved by formation of translaminar electron layer through the choice of the optimal voltages for the control electrode and electron beam inhibition by the electrostatic field of the collector. This approach allowed for dense electron grouping in nonlaminar electron beams that provided the growth of the amplitude of the higher harmonics in the output power spectrum. In this system, the increase of the fundamental operating frequency by application of external magnetic field was experimentally demonstrated. If combined with higher harmonics generation mode, this can lead to significant increase of resulting operating frequency of the compact low-voltage system to millimeter wavelength band.

articleTitle: Low-Temperature-grown GaAs photoconductors suitable for 1550nm-wavelength illumination
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this communication, we show that ultrafast photoconductors based on low-temperature-grown Gallium Arsenide material exhibit photoresponse values reaching 11 mA/W under 1550 nm CW excitation. This is obtained by using an optical microcavity based on a buried metal layer acting as back reflecting mirror and a top grating electrode in order to improve the external quantum efficiency and by decreasing the post growth annealing temperature of the LT-GaAs layer downto 450 °C. Frequency response measurements are carried out up to 67 GHz by using a 1550-nm-wavelength optical-heterodyne experiment.

articleTitle: Enhanced THz signal via Au encapsulated in hydrogel gel for non-enzymatic glucose sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Non-enzymatic glucose sensors were developed based on Au nanoparticles embedded in the hydrogel system. The sensors were soaked in glucose aqueous solutions with concentrations ranging from 0 to 1.5 mg/mL for 30 min. Terahertz time domain spectroscopy was then used to measure the absorption of the sensors. The Au nanoparticles can oxidize the glucose molecules to gluconic acid, resulting in a pH change of the samples. The sensitivity of the sensors to glucose levels are therefore enhanced compared to traditional terahertz spectroscopy measurements.

articleTitle: SiGe Based LNA for Data Communication Applications at 211 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the use of a silicon based 211 GHz preamplifier for THz links. A test bench setup is assembled to evaluate the performance of the amplifier using a uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) as the source of a 5Gbps modulated signal. The Bit Error Rate curve was extracted versus the input power, with and without the amplifier. It is verified that the system margin in the BER curve is improved in relation with the amplifier gain. The use of the silicon based active stage is a proof of concept for next-generation wireless communication systems above 200 GHz leveraging industrial silicon technologies.

articleTitle: Long-Range Non-Line of Sight THz Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz spectrum is an emerging and promising spectrum as it provides sub-mm spatial resolution and many materials have unique fingerprints at this frequency range. However, the THz spectra suffer from high atmospheric absorption and free space path loss, limiting the propagation range. State-of-the-art THz testbed demonstrations with a bandwidth of >100 GHz are focused on a line of sight (LoS) sensing and limited to a propagation range of sub-2 m. This paper demonstrates non-LoS sensing up to the fifth order of reflection for the frequency band of 220-330 GHz with a range of >6 m.

articleTitle: Terahertz waveform selection of a pharmaceutical film coating process using a recurrent network
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Waveform selection plays an important role in the processing of in-line terahertz measurements of pharmaceutical tablet coating processes. This paper presents an approach to optimise waveform selection by utilising an artificial recurrent neural network and transfer learning. The results show that the averaged coating thickness gradually increases throughout the coating process. In comparison with the conventional method, our approach allows more than double the number of waveforms to be selected without compromising on the accuracy when compared against off-line measurements. Moreover, the processing time of waveform selection decreases so that it can be applied for real-time coating monitor in the pharmaceutical industry.

articleTitle: A Novel THz Metasurface Sensor Based on the Integration of Carbon Nanotube Film and Grating Silicon Microfluidic Channel
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel design for THz metasurface sensor based on the integration of carbon nanotube film (CNTs) and grating silicon (G-Si) microfluidic channel is proposed. Two obvious resonant absorption peaks located at 0.93 THz and 1.66 THz, the absorption is nearly 83.4% and 99.7%, respectively. Owing to the coupling of the CNTs and G-Si, a higher quality factor (Q) is obtained at the resonance absorption peak. The electric and magnetic field distribution of the resonance absorption peaks were investigated. The proposed novel THz metasurface sensor can be used for sensing various solutions with different refractive index flowing into the microfluidic channel.

articleTitle: Design of a TE11 - TE21 Mode Converter Based on a Three-fold Helically Corrugated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The mode converter based on a helically corrugated waveguide (HCW) presented in this paper is an important component for a gyrotron traveling wave amplifier. A three-fold right-handed (HCW) has been designed, which converted a left-hand circular polarized (CP) TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode to a right-hand CP TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> mode in the frequency range of 258-268 GHz. It achieved a transmission coefficient of better than -0.3 dB and a reflection below -30 dB.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Spectral Fusion Terahertz Deep Learning Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel method to visualize 3D object details through a multi-band spectral fusion deep learning approach. This method, multi-dominant-band spatio-spectral fusion network (MS-Unet), incorporates rich information from multi-frequency band spectral data. The reconstructed terahertz tomographic images significantly outperform conventional methods, enhancing 8.97 dB in PSNR, boosting SSIM from 0.05 to 0.70, and improving LPIPS from 0.36 to 0.18.

articleTitle: Integrated resonant cavities on substrateless terahertz dielectric waveguide platform
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present two resonant cavity designs for an all-silicon substrateless dielectric waveguide platform based on effective medium implementation. These include a disk resonator and a photonic crystal cavity. The substrateless dielectric waveguide platform realizes very low absorption that is beneficial to achieve a high-Q resonance for these cavities. The measurement results of the disk resonator show a Q-factor of 559 at 276.3 GHz, while the photonic crystal cavity show strong resonance behavior and high transmission at 279.8 GHz. Additionally, the photoconductive tuning of the resonance of these cavities is demonstrated. The 276.3 GHz disk resonator and the 279.8 GHz photonic crystal cavity both show strong tunability of the resonance when selected parts are illuminated with moderate optical power. These cavities can be employed in various terahertz applications including sensing, switching, and modulation.

articleTitle: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Biosensor Chips for Label-Free Detection of Ovarian Cancer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A new diagnosis approach for ovarian cancer (OC) based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated, which is label-free, damage-free, and sensitive. SPPs exhibit high electric field confinement and non-diffraction limit. Due to the resonance of split ring resonators (SRRs), the proposed device further enhances the localized field and thus achieves high sensitivity for biosensing. Normal ovarian, serous ovarian cancer, and ovarian clear cell carcinoma tissues were mounted on the SRRs for detection, and different frequency shifting of 90, 212, and 203 MHz was observed, respectively. This approach may also be suitable for diagnosis of other cancerous tissues.

articleTitle: Novel Radial Power Combiner/Divider Based on Circular Sectoral Waveguide TE01 Mode
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel W-band radial power combiner/divider based on circular sectoral waveguide TE01 mode is presented in this paper. By analyzing the field distribution characteristics of the circular sectoral waveguide, we designed an equal amplitude and in-phase power combiner/divider which consists of a circular sectoral waveguide TE01-mode transducer and a 6-way power divider. In the 88-97 GHz frequency range, the measured insertion loss of this power combiner/divider is less than 0.75dB and the measured return loss at the input port is better than 20dB.
