This power/divider can reduce the order of the operating mode and has better mode rejection and compact size than the circular waveguide TE01 mode power combiner/divider, and can be scaled to the terahertz frequency band.

articleTitle: Planar Integrated MMW/THz Antennas Based on Higher-Order Mode Cavity and Printed Circuit Board Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a planar substrate integrated MMW/THz antenna is presented using a higher-order mode feeding cavity and modified radiation apertures. The antenna is directly fed by a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW). The GCPW is separated into two slots at the terminal to respectively excite two parallel TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">201</inf> resonant cavities and realize a 2×2 slot array. The antenna structure is improved using modified radiation apertures for the purpose of modified radiation patterns and higher antenna gain. A 60 GHz band antenna is fabricated and measured. The measured peak gain is 14.6 dBi with a 3-dB gain bandwidth from 53.2 to 65.8 GHz (21.2%). In addition, based on the proposed structure and printed circuit board technology, a THz band antenna is explored and designed with a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 24.4%, from 0.18 to 0.23 THz.

articleTitle: Power Enhancement of 38 GHz Sheet Beam EIO by Field Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A compact high power extended interaction oscillator (EIO) is studied with an aim to increase its output power. The cavity is designed, so that its transverse mode is TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>and the longitudinal mode is 2π and the operating frequency is 38 GHz. The modulating E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> field is optimized in such a way that it varies ascendingly in the growing z-direction. This gradually growing E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> -field has been found, to have a positive impact on sheet-beam EIO output performance in terms of its output power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> and beam-wave interaction efficiency. To incorporate the negative influence of skin effect and surface roughness on the output performance the conductivity of background material is taken one-fourth of that of pure copper σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Cu</inf>. After field optimization the final design output power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> is predicted to improve from 20.19 kW to 24.98 kW and efficiency is improved from 33% to 40.83%.

articleTitle: Super resolution of a 400 MHz rotational line doublet with a TDS using a 850 ps long delay line
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We improved the spectral resolution of THz time domain spectroscopy beyond the limit given by the delay line length. The constraint reconstruction algorithm used successfully depicted the 1.21 THz NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> doublet separated by ~400MHz in experimental data despite the 1.2 GHz delay line limitation.

articleTitle: Investigation of Cross-Section Measurement Method for All-Solid-State Batteries Using Terahertz Chemical Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In recent years, all-solid-state batteries have been attracting attention as secondary batteries to replace Li ion batteries. To improve the performance of all-solid-state batteries, measurement methods are required to evaluate electrode-solid electrolyte interfaces and electrochemical reactions between electrodes. In this study, we investigated a measurement method for the cross-section of all-solid-state batteries using terahertz chemical microscopy (TCM). We fabricated a model of all-solid-state battery and showed the possibility of using TCM to measure the cross-section of the all-solid-state battery by measuring the cross-section of a model of all-solid-state battery.

articleTitle: Small Variation of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Concentration Can Be Observed with THz Frequency Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz frequency domain spectroscopy (THzFDS) has been employed to study the result of variation of active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) on the effective refractive index of pharmaceutical tablets. A quasi-optical set-up with four off-axis parabolic mirrors was used to measure the effective refractive index of tablets in the frequency range of 500-750 GHz. It was observed that a small variation in API concentration can be detected using accurate measurements of the complex transmission coefficients. As a results, THz-FDS reveals to be an effective technique in monitoring the physical properties of pharmaceutical tablets.

articleTitle: Raman Spectroscopy of Sucrose, D(+) Glucose and D(-) Fructose in Terahertz and Infrared Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Molecular recognition and discrimination of organic compounds are important because hydrogen bonds and hydrogen-bonding interactions in organic compounds (especially carbohydrates) perform essential roles in energy metabolism and medical diagnosis. We investigate the Raman spectroscopy of sucrose, D(+) glucose and D(-) fructose in the terahertz and infrared frequency ranges. Sucrose consists of fructose and glucose rings and absorption bands specific for sucrose only are identified at ~1553 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and ~2679 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Energy of the absorption band at ~3570 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is affected by crystalline fields and is different for these three compounds measured.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Cosmetic Liquid Penetration Using Terahertz Time-of-Flight Method
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: It is important to evaluate the penetration depth and speed of cosmetics into the skin for the cosmetic industry. However, the conventional method for measuring those parameters has some drawbacks. In this study, a terahertz time-of-flight method with Si-based emitter was applied for evaluation. The penetration of the liquid into a pig skin was measured as a travelling time of the THz pulses irradiating on a pigskin, where the glycerin concentration in the liquid was varied.

articleTitle: 2 MW ECRH System for ST40 Spherical Tokamak
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A multi-frequency electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and current drive (CD) system is currently under construction at the ST40 spherical tokamak. The system employs 2 GYCOM gyrotrons with a maximum output power of 1 MW each and a pulse length of 2s. Both gyrotrons can be tuned to operate either at 105 GHz or 140 GHz. The system is designed to study a non-inductive plasma start-up, current ramp-up and sustainment.

articleTitle: Compressed FTIR spectroscopy for scanning based methods
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectral imaging spatially distributed spectra of 2D surfaces are registered simultaneously using FTIR spectrometers equipped with array detectors. Scanning methods such as near-field FTIR spectroscopy are a promising alternative providing both, higher spatial resolution, and sensitivity. However, serial recording severely limits their imaging application due to long acquisition times involved and the resulting stability issues. In this work we demonstrate different strategies to compress the FTIR measurement already at the data acquisition stage to significantly reduce the measurement time. Corresponding reconstruction schemes and their hardware implementation will be discussed.

articleTitle: Wide frequency-tunable 1 THz resonant tunneling diode oscillator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The compact and high-performance resonant tunneling diode oscillator has great potential in terahertz applications. In this work, we report a 1 THz resonant tunneling diode (RTD) oscillator with wide frequency tuning range from 935 GHz to 1.035 THz (100 GHz) under the voltage change of 0.5-0.62 V within its negative differential conductance (NDC) range, which is due to the improvement of RTD heterojunction structure.

articleTitle: Detection of cancer cells using immune reaction with a terahertz chemical microscope
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Recently, analyzing cancer genome is attracted to personalize cancer treatment. The ratio of cancer cells in a specimen is essential for precise analysis of the genome. In our group, a terahertz chemical microscope (TCM) has been proposed and developed to measure the number of cancer cells in solution. In this study, a biotin-tagged AE1/AE3 was immobilized on a sensing plate using avidin-biotin reaction, and we succeed in detecting lung cancer cells in solutions.

articleTitle: The Study of Traveling Wave Tube Large Signal Model Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Driven by success in areas such as computer vision and natural language processing, attempts have been made in this work to combine deep learning with the large signal of the Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) to assist in predicting the output performance of the tube and advancing the pre-design of TWT. By feeding the trained artificial neural network with several feature parameters, the output power with the tube length can be predicted.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of a Terahertz TE20 Mode Input/Output Coupling Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Preliminary study of a TE20 input/output coupling structure for sheet electron beam traveling wave tubes is presented in this paper. A TE10-TE20 mode converter and a single branch waveguide coupler are used to realize the proposed design. Simulation results obtained by using the CST simulation software demonstrated that the port reflection and the transmission coefficient were respectively lower than - 15 dB and higher than - 1 dB in the frequency range of 241-298 GHz. The port isolation was lower than - 10 dB in the frequency range of 250-298 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Photonics with Terahertz Semiconductor Lasers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) generation using photonic techniques has so far been limited to the use of near-infrared lasers that are down-converted to the mmWave region. However, such methodologies do not currently benefit from a monolithic architecture and suffer from the quantum defect. Here we show how miniaturized terahertz (THz) quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) can open up the possibility of innovatively integrating both laser action and mmWave generation in a single device. We demonstrate intracavity mmWave generation within THz QCLs over the unprecedented range of 25 GHz to 500 GHz using their inherent giant nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Terahertz Broadband RCS Reduction Enhancement by Polarization Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband and high-efficiency RCS reduction enhancement by employing a polarization-conversion coding metasurface is demonstrated in the terahertz region. A symmetric linearly polarized conversion metasurface with a relative bandwidth of 74% and a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) over 90% from 0.24 THz to 0.52 THz is designed as the 1-bit coding block. By applying the Golay-Rudin-Shapiro (GRS) polynomials on the coding series, a highly effective RCS reduction paradigm averaged below -20 dB has been achieved with a cross-polarization enhancement. Compared to the co-polarized counterpart, a -10 dB enhancement is attained by the cross-polarized coding array. It paves a promising path to terahertz RCS reduction and polarized wave regulation.

articleTitle: Circuit-Based Design and Optimization for Broadband Terahertz Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a semi-analytical approach incorporating network analysis and genetic algorithm to facilitate the design and optimization of broadband transmissive metasurfaces. For verification, three broadband metasurface-based devices are rigorously designed following the optimal circuit parameters provided by the approach. The presented broadband approach can be employed to configure diverse metasurfaces that locally alter the magnitude, phase, and polarization states of terahertz waves so to support wideband terahertz applications.

articleTitle: Impact of the Local Oscillator on High-Bandwidth Millimeter-Wave Communication Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The application of mixers is essential for the use of frequencies in the millimeter-wave band. They are needed to convert modulated baseband signals to the desired transmission band. In this work, the influence of the local oscillator in magnitude and phase on the error vector magnitude of a broadband signal will be investigated. For this purpose, an arbitrary waveform generator is used to generate a broadband modulated signal in the baseband, which is up-converted and transmitted over a 300 GHz transmission link with a variable local oscillator and then evaluated by a real time oscilloscope after down-conversion.

articleTitle: Accurately frequency-resolved air-plasma THz beam profile from knifeedge assisted waveform measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate accurately frequency-resolved profile measurement for a two-color air-plasma THz beam. It was achieved by combining THz waveform measurements and the knife-edge technique. The measurements show that while high frequencies feature a hollow donut shape, the low frequency beam is very close to a Gaussian profile.

articleTitle: Initiation of THz Spherical Wave of Electron Bunch near Metallic Boundary
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spatio-temporal measurement of THz spherical wave generated by the electron bunch passing across a metallic foil was conducted. Transverse THz electric field around a relativistic sub-picosecond electron bunch was measured using electro-optic (EO) sampling based on balance detection. The shape of the spherical wavefront was changed by adjusting the longitudinal position of the metallic foil which reflects THz electric field around the electron bunch before passing across the foil. Experimentally obtained field map was compared with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: THz electrometry with Rydberg atoms and all IR lasers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and Autler-Townes (AT) splitting in an atomic vapor cell can be used as novel methods for electric-magnetic field detection. Here we make use of 3 infrared lasers to realize a Rydberg EIT system in a thermal rubidium vapor cell. With the AT splitting induced by the THz radiation, we observe a linear trend between THz field amplitude and the frequency splitting of the absorption dips and EIT transmission peaks. Due to the well-known atomic transition dipole moment of the Rydberg state, the THz electric field can be calibrated from the frequency splitting, making this Rydberg atomic measurement system a practical tool for THz field detection.

articleTitle: Guidance of Terahertz Wave over Commercial Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work proposes a new flexible terahertz subwavelength fiber using commercial optical fiber as the core medium. The proposed dual-band fiber allows the optical signals to propagate in the innermost two layers and the THz signal to distributed over the optical fiber and mostly in the lossless foam cladding. The propagation loss at 1550 nm and 500 μm are 0.2 dB/km and 0.034 dB/mm, respectively. The proposed fiber is compact and cost-effective, making it a promising candidate for optical and terahertz fusion sensing, imaging, and nonlinear optoelectronics applications.

articleTitle: Mode Interaction in Clinotron with Periodically Modified Grating
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The interaction of the modes with different variations along grating lamella occurring in a clinotron with periodically modified grating due to the profile of the clinotron circuit cross-section, has been studied. The simulation results demonstrate the interaction of the sheet electron beam with two modes, which differ in the transverse index, at the same frequency.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Solar Observation Lunar Volatiles Experiment (SSOLVE) Optics and Front-end Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: SSOLVE is a heterodyne spectrometer that is under development as a technology demonstration for future lunar lander missions. The system contains a heliostat to target the Sun, optics, and submillimeter-wave, and Terahertz (THz) receivers to measure the column abundance of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, OH, and HDO.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Absorption and Shielding based on 2D materials
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: With the development of terahertz (THz) technology, there is a booming demand of THz shielding/absorption materials to avoid electromagnetic interference (EMI) or pollution. Here, we report on a series of THz absorption or shielding materials fabricated from 2D MXene nanosheets. By using simple dip-coating or spray-coating method, lightweight, flexible, thin, and hydrophobic absorption foam are obtained, which shows ultrahigh THz absorption property over 99.99% under the 100% qualified frequency bandwidth ranging from 0.3 to 1.65 THz. Our results indicate that the combination of 2D materials with porous polymer paves a way to achieving high performance THz absorber, which is of significance in electromagnetic interference shielding, 6G communications and beyond.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of a 210-220 GHz Manifold Triplexer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a 220-GHz triplexer which is composed of three Chebyshev bandpass filters. Through co-design of low-order electromagnetic (EM) distributed models and full-wave EM models, the design optimization is achieved with a good computational efficiency and design accuracy. The proposed triplexer is fabricated by computer numerical control (CNC) milling technology, which exhibits less than 3 dB of in-band insertion loss and better than 10 dB of average common-port return loss for each channel. The measured results are all in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry of InSb in the Terahertz Region
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Herein we show the terahertz (THz) time-domain ellipsometry investigation of the InSb semiconductor. At room temperature, the carriers of InSb are thermally excited to the conduction band due to its narrow bandgap. We, nevertheless, show that THz ellipsometry can detect subtle differences between carrier densities of undoped and lightly doped InSb bulk semiconductors. The advantage of THz ellipsometry over other THz time-domain spectroscopy techniques is that it does not require reference measurements through an aperture or standard mirrors.

articleTitle: Terahertz and Infrared Spectroscopy of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Spectral properties of S and S1 spike proteins were studied using vibration spectroscopy methods. Also, vibration signatures of amino acids that make up the RGD, the part of S1 protein responsible for adhesion, were studied by Terahertz (THz) time-domain, Infrared (IR) and Raman spectroscopies in the low-frequency and in the fingerprint. THz metamaterials have been developed that increase the sensitivity of THz spectroscopy to the presence of both proteins. We have studied the spectra of amino acids, which play a role in the adhesion of proteins, on the metal surfaces of metamaterials, aluminum, and gold. Spectral differences were found between S and S1 proteins of SARS-CoV-2. The spectral differences between amino acids prepared in the form of thin films and in the form of bulk sample are discussed.

articleTitle: Antenna designs for near field waveguide coupling between 0.6 – 0.9 THz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dielectric waveguide architectures enable low loss, miniaturized terahertz systems-on-chip with extreme bandwidth. However, transfer of power from active devices to the waveguides presents a severe challenge. In this paper, we present a comparison of two Vivaldi end-fire antenna designs with losses of 2 – 5 dB per coupling interface to silicon waveguides over a frequency range as large as 0.6 – 0.9 THz. We demonstrate lower losses between 0.63 – 0.83 THz as compared to far field in-coupling with silicon lenses, despite being orders of magnitude smaller in size.

articleTitle: Phase Control of Injection-Locked RTD Terahertz Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We constructed a heterodyne system for measuring the phase of terahertz (THz) waves with high accuracy and achieved to control the phase of a resonant tunneling diode (RTD) oscillator using injection locking. The free-running oscillation frequency of the RTD THz oscillator was tuned from 380.5 to 386.7 GHz in the bias range of 0.61-0.65 V. In the phase measurement, we injected a signal of 383.2 GHz to the RTD THz oscillator and measured the phase with different free-running frequencies. The phase changed almost from −90° to +90° within the locking range, which agrees with the expectation derived from Adler's equation.

articleTitle: Integrated Terahertz Tunneling Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a novel in-slab beamforming technique that leverages optical tunneling and leaky-wave phenomena. In this way, a frequency-scanning focused beam is projected into a micro-scale silicon slab, and by collecting this beam at a single point with an inverse flare, an integrated all-intrinsic-silicon filter is realized. This technique holds great potential to realize efficient, broadband, all-dielectric frequency-division multiplexers for terahertz, infrared, and visible-frequency waves.

articleTitle: Development of a 3D Imaging System Using Millimeter Wave MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We performed 3D imaging of a clothed human using a single millimeter-wave MIMO radar. By performing clustering and smoothing processes based on the observed intermediate frequency signals, 3D image reconstruction was successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Polarization-insensitive InGaAs-based THz plasmonic photomixers based on subwavelength meshes
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we designed and simulated a polarization-insensitive InGaAs-based Continues wave THz emitter. In the proposed structure, the metallic meshes geometry is designed to increase optical transmission to the active area near the contact electrodes. The nanometer structured metallic features also enhance the local bias field near contact edges where the most photoexcited carriers are generated, leading to enhanced THz current. The simulation results demonstrate that the optimized structure generates 51 μw THz power under unpolarized 200 mW optical pump power at 500 GHz beat frequency.

articleTitle: Radiative Reference Plane Estimation and Uncertainty for THz Path Loss Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A line-of-sight VNA measurement over 300 – 310 GHz with a separation of 10 – 340 cm, at 10 cm intervals was performed. The rms difference between the VNA results and Friis losses, calculated from distance measurements and Power-Delay Profile, was used to optimize the radiative reference plane correction. Optimal results were 10.1 mm (distance measurement) and 8.9 mm (PDP) for each antenna. This correction is significant for separations below 1 m.

articleTitle: Organic Semiconductors as High-Speed Photoconductive Terahertz Spatial Light Modulators
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we present the first study on organic semiconductors as a photoconductive terahertz spatial light modulator (THz SLM), to the best of the authors’ knowledge. The characterization includes modulation depth (MD) created by the photocarriers within the material and the measurement of carrier lifetime, relating to the operation speed of the material. We observed 16.50% of MD, and the carrier lifetime was measured to be 4.527 ns. As the carrier lifetime is similar to gallium arsenide (GaAs), we compare both and discover an order of magnitude enhancement in MD. This report shows that organic semiconductors can serve as a promising high-speed THz SLM for real-time terahertz imaging.

articleTitle: Complex refractive indices in the TeraHertz domain of samples from atmospheric aerosol sources
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report the TeraHertz (THz) characterization of calcium carbonate (CaCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) particles, one of the major components of desert dust, to determine the real and imaginary parts of their complex refractive indices. The optical characterization is done by TeraHertz Time Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) technique. CaCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders are diluted with High Density PolyEthylene (PE) at different concentrations (0.1% to 75% of CaCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and compressed in pellets. Time-traces are then fitted using the Fit@TDS algorithm developed by Photonic TeraHertz group members, and the complex refractive indices are extracted. We support the optical characterization by a morphological characterization by Scanning Electron Microscopy - Energy Dispersive X-Ray (SEM-EDX) analysis after resuspension of particles and filtration on a polycarbonate 0.2 µm pore filter.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Lens Horn Antenna for Fixed-Beam D-Band Backhaul Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized plane-convex lens horn antenna for fixed-beam backhaul systems developed by Anteral. The frequency range of 130/160 GHz (D-band) which is perspective for the future point-to-point 6G communications is covered. The antenna is fed by a high-performance orthomode transducer (OMT) to provide with horizontal and vertical linear polarizations. The measured directivity of the antenna (11 cm diameter aperture size) exceeds 40 dBi and the sidelobe suppression in both E and H planes is above 30 dB. The cross-polar level is below 30 dB at boresight and the isolation between the vertical and horizontal polarized signals is around 50 dB.

articleTitle: Optical path length measurement of spherical dielectric shells with axicon-generated Bessel beams; applications to corneal sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A custom aspheric axicon lens for corneal water content sensing, operating from 220 to 330 GHz, was evaluated with spherical, dielectric shell targets. The lens consisted of a hyperbolic back surface and conical front surface with a 25-degree axicon angle. An 8 mm radius of curvature, 1 mm thick, air backed dome was placed in the beam path and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> acquired at numerous axial offsets between dome and axicon. The data was normalized by equivalent radius of curvature metallic spherical reflectors. Fits to reflectivity data ranged from ε = 4.1 and t = 0.89 mm and ε = 4.16 and t = 0.885 for lens-tip to shell-apex distances of 34 mm and 25 mm respectively. The results suggest that Bessel beam illumination may relax axial alignment constraints in THz imaging of cornea.

articleTitle: Project of 30 GHz Compact Low-voltage Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The possibility of developing a simple, low-voltage 30 GHz gyrotron packaged in warm magnet with moderate power consumption is discussed. For various operating modes, the design of both gyrotron tube and magnetic system are analyzed. Based on the tradeoff between microwave output power and magnet powerconsumption, the modes TE01 and TE12 are chosen due to acceptable efficiency and small diameter of magnet bore. According to simulations, the gyrotron with the operating voltage of 5 kV can provide 250 W of output power.

articleTitle: Development of Photoinjector Complex in IAP RAS: Design of Accelerating Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A two-stage accelerator complex based on the photoinjection gun is under development in the Institute of Applied Physics at present. It is designed to accelerate the electron bunches with a charge of up to 100 pC to the particle energy of ~3–5 MeV after the first stage and ~20 MeV after the second stage. The report presents the design and design parameters of the accelerating microwave sections, as well as the results of "cold" testing of the first stage key components.

articleTitle: Stable and scalable two-stage terahertz-driven particle accelerator
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz technology can largely reduce the cost and size of conventional accelerators. Here, we demonstrate a stable two-stage mini-accelerator powered by 20-period terahertz pulses. By tuning the frequency of narrowband terahertz, phase matching was achieved between terahertz and a short relativistic electron bunch in a 30mm dielectric tube. Under the circumstance of precisely controlling the phase of two terahertz pulses, the beam is stably accelerated successively in two dielectric tubes for nearly 100% charge coupling efficiency with beam energy spread essentially unchanged. Our results mark a great step from advanced acceleration to advanced accelerator and pave the way for functioning terahertz-driven high-energy accelerators.

articleTitle: Total-Variation Iterative Algorithm for Terahertz Transmission Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 3D continuous-wave (CW) terahertz computed tomography (CT) system employing a terahertz sources (IMPATT diodes) operating at 278.6 GHz is presented. To shorten acquisition time on the premise of guaranteeing the image quality, the algorithm minimizes the total variation (TV) is used to reconstruct the THz-CT results of zero order Bessel beam. With the 2D results of the samples have been also obtained.

articleTitle: Automatic terahertz recognition of hidden defects in layered polymer composites based on a deep residual network with transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a deep residual network with transfer learning strategy for automatic terahertz (THz) recognition of the hidden defects in fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites with small-scale training data. The recognition performance with high accuracy, precision, sensitivity and specificity indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method for automatically identifying different defects in THz nondestructive applications.

articleTitle: Observation of Atomic Oxygen in the Mesosphere and Thermosphere of Earth with the THz Heterodyne Spectrometer GREAT
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Atomic oxygen governs photochemistry and energy balance of the mesosphere and lower thermosphere of the Earth. Its concentration is extremely difficult to measure with remote sensing techniques since it has only few optically active transitions. Current indirect measurements involve photochemical models and the results are not always in agreement, particularly when obtained with different instruments. In addition, altitudes above 100 km are not covered by these methods. We report on direct measurements of the 4.7-THz fine-structure transition of atomic oxygen at 4.7448 THz using the German Receiver for Astronomy at Terahertz Frequencies on board the Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy. Our measurements agree well with atmospheric models and satellite observations below 100 km.

articleTitle: 300GHz Terahertz Transmission Scheme Based on SFP Optical Fiber Module
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents a fusion of optical fiber transmission with terahertz wireless communication system scheme. One of a pair of SFP optical module is used to process the digital signal generated by AWG (arbitrary waveform generator), which is transmitted by optical fiber for long distance. Another SFP optical module completes the photoelectric conversion of the signal and inputs the signal to the terahertz frequency conversion module for wireless transmission. The code rate is 1.25 Gbps, the carrier frequency is 300 GHz and the modulation mode is QPSK. The results were observed through the eye diagram of the signal received by the oscilloscope. The quality of the eye diagram is well, which indicates that the terahertz over fiber wireless communication has practical significance for indoor high-speed access and other application scenarios.

articleTitle: rGO Based Ultrathin Broadband Terahertz Absorbing Paper
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Utilizing the in-situ reducing method, a reduced graphene oxide (rGO) paper for 13~14 um was obtained and exhibits great Terahertz (THz) absorbing capability. The absorption of rGO paper exceeds 43% in the whole frequency band from 0.3~1.2 THz and maximum absorption reaches 59.33% at 1.13 THz. This makes it possible to realize ultra-thin broadband THz absorbing materials.

articleTitle: Outdoor multi-polarization passive millimeter–wave imaging via integrated W-band dual polarization direct detection radiometer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: we describe the design and phenomenology imaging results of an integrated W-band dual polarization direct detection radiometer developed by ‘TeraFuture laboratory’ for outdoor multi-polarization passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) imaging. Operating from 75GHz~110GHz, the integrated W-band radiometer, which shows a high level of integration and is easy-to-use, has two same channels while each channel can receive two orthogonal polarization states of the incident millimeter-wave (MMW) radiation simultaneously. Based on the radiometer, an outdoor multi-polarization PMMW image system has been build, whose image angular resolution is less than 0.4°. Multi-polarization measurements are realized by rotating the detector around the observation axis direction. A large outdoor area has been imaged, which include the buildings, vegetative cover, personal cars and cement road, egg. Various polarization parameter images are generated to analyze the polarization characteristics and the images are compared between in and after the rain. The results show that the multi-polarization imaging has the great potential for remote sensing.

articleTitle: Deep learning approach for analysis of terahertz quantum cascade lasers with distributed feedback
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel approach based on deep neural networks is introduced to perform both efficient and accurate predictions of frequency, loss and electric-field distributions for the lowest-loss resonant mode in terahertz quantum cascade lasers (THz QCLs) with distributed feedback (DFB). The designed neural networks show promising results on various types of DFB structures in THz QCLs, including 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-order, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>-order DFB and antenna-feedback schemes. Compared with conventional numerical simulations, the running time of our proposed methods is significantly decreased. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of fast and precise predictions for resonant mode characteristics in THz QCLs utilizing deep learning.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metasurface Spectrum Prediction Based On Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metasurface, a two-dimensional periodic artificial electromagnetic material, usually composed of metal/medium or all medium. It has become a popular research area due to its unique electromagnetic properties. However, due to the complex modeling and electromagnetic simulation, the study of the electromagnetic characteristics of terahertz metasurface is time-consuming. To solve this problem, we introduced deep learning method to explore and optimize the terahertz metasurface design process. We constructed a terahertz metasurface structure, and obtained a small part of spectral data in the whole sample space through software simulation, and then put these data into the neural network for learning. By verifying the trained neural network, the spectral information of terahertz mteasurface with different structural parameters can be predicted. This method can help us to simplify the design process of metasurface.

articleTitle: Development of Ion Concentration Measurement Method for Minute Volume of Blood Using Terahertz Chemical Microscope
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A terahertz chemical microscope (TCM) was proposed and developed to measure small ion concentrations in solution. By creating multiple wells on the sensing plate, it was possible to measure the ion concentration of 35 μl of whole sheep blood.

articleTitle: Fast Time Response of THz detection in JLFET
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The speed of detectors represents a crucial point in the definition of the communication system using THz carrier. Rectification performed by MOS structures was usually detected by lock-in amplifiers, thus appears quite slow. We show by theoretical analysis and TCAD simulations that JLFET is intrinsically very fast, and that velocity may increase by a new approach of detection through the gate capacitance charging. The experimental results confirm the conclusions.

articleTitle: Extremely high Q-factor terahertz metamaterial microfluidic sensor based on InN Strips
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose an extremely high Q-factor terahertz metamaterial microfluidic sensor based on semiconductor materials. The unit cell consists of four layers: Au baseboard, dielectric and InN strips mixed layer, InN slab and a cover dielectric layer. Excellent sensing characteristics have been achieved with a high quality-factor (Q-factor) of 199.6 and an absorbance of 96.1% at 4.672 THz, the RI sensitivities reaches 1251GHz/RIU.

articleTitle: New Series of Standards VDI/VDE 5590 on Terahertz Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In 2013, members of the terahertz community in Germany initiated the formation of VDI standards for terahertz systems. Since terahertz systems are associated with different research branches, the initiative serves, among other aspects, to develop a consistent language and to map transparent quality characteristics for an emerging technology. We report on our ongoing work within this initiative and address the challenges involved. While the standards are also published in English and are internationally accessible, it is desirable to address future initiatives also in the context of international collaborations.

articleTitle: Selective Strongly Oversized Resonators for Powerful Free-Electron Lasers Operating from Sub-THz to THz Band
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Project of sub-THz/THz band FEL driven by linac "LIU" 5 - 20 MeV / 2 kA / 200 ns is under development in collaboration between BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (N.Novgorod). This project is aimed to achieve sub-GW power and a record pulse energy content of ~ 10 -100 J in this frequency range. In order to provide stable narrow-band generation regime in the strongly-oversized oscillator, we elaborate two types of electrodynamic systems: (1) advanced Bragg resonators based on coupling of quasi-cutoff and propagating waves and (2) quasi-optical resonators of the Talbot-type. Design of these resonators, their simulations and "cold" test results are presented, state of the project is discussed.

articleTitle: Rapid Identification of THz Tags using Multi-wavelength is-TPG based on a Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a practical THz tag reading system by combining a multi-wavelength injection-seeded terahertz parametric generator (is-TPG) with machine learning by deep neural networks. Reagent pellets with clear fingerprint spectra were used as the THz tag.

articleTitle: Terahertz Detection by an Asymmetric Dual-Grating-Gate Graphene FET
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on fast, sensitive terahertz (THz) detection in an asymmetric dual-grating-gate graphene channel field-effect transistor (ADGG-GFET). Bias-dependent photoresponse is measured to clearly identify the plasmonic and photo-thermoelectric rectification mechanisms that could co-exist while preserving picosecond response speed.

articleTitle: A criterion to compare permittivity models in the terahertz range
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a method to take experimental noise in THz-TDS into account during the fitting process. With its implementation in our software fit@TDS, we were able to fit accurately the spectrum of the golden sample: a lactose pellet.

articleTitle: Recent Results of 28 GHz 400 kW Long Pulse Gyrotrons at IAE-CAEP
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Recently, 28GHz, 400kW gyrotrons have been built and tested at IAE-CAEP. The gyrotrons were developed for ECRH experiments with a spherical tokamak. The gyrotrons have a single anode magnetron injection gun to produce gyrating electron beam. The operational cavity mode is TE8,3, which is converted into a Gaussian mode by an internal quasi-optical mode converter. In order to enhance the overall efficiency, single stage depressed collectors are used. In the test, output frequency of the gyrotron is 28.1 GHz. With the cathode voltage -52kV, anode voltage about 20 kV, excited by different beam currents, the gyrotron (#2) has realized long pulse, high power output of 200 kW / 5 s, 300 kW / 3 s, and 400 kW / 1 s. Another tube (gyrotron #3) has been tested in May and delivered 400 kW / 5 s output power on May 21, 2021. Now the gyrotrons have been installed on the spherical tokamak and successfully used as trial products in the ECRH experiment. Further test of several optimized gyrotrons will continue during the next several months.

articleTitle: Analysis of 220-GHz Communication Link Using A High-Order Direct-Modulation Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, an RF direct-modulation transmitter (Tx) architecture for high-speed wireless transmission is presented, which directly maps the data bits to 4M quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellation. The basic principle is to vectorially synthesize M channels of QPSK modulated signals with proportional amplitudes, thereby realizing high-order QAM modulation and avoiding the use of costly digital-to-analog converters (DACs). We have designed a 220GHz sub-harmonic mixer and a 3dB branch waveguide coupler, and then built a TX three-dimensional circuit model with a carrier frequency of 220 GHz and 16QAM direct modulation, and carried out a communication link simulation verification.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Crossed Dipole Resonator Array using a Pulsed Free Space Two-Port Photonic VNA
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a Photonic Vector Network Analyzer (PVNA) capable of measuring a complete set of scattering parameters within the frequency range of 0.2 – 2 THz. The PVNA shows superiority in terms of bandwidth compared to electrical VNAs and is also free from the errors introduced by standing waves, metal waveguides, misaligned flanges, and features less stringent requirements on rigorous and time-consuming calibration routines. As a proof of principle, we characterize a crossed dipole resonator array using the free space two-port PVNA.

articleTitle: Automated Material Map Generation for Terahertz Images based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, an approach for automated material mapping based on neural networks for terahertz images is proposed. The classification method is applied on focused transmission measurements of a terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system for 13 different 3-D printed polymers. With our approach, a classification accuracy of around 95 % was achieved.

articleTitle: Ultra-low Threshold Quantum Cascade Laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Semiconductor lasers with ultra-low thresholds and minimal footprints are a topic of active research. Such devices require a combination of high quality factor laser cavities with small active region volumes. For high-reflectivity coated ridge lasers, a low threshold can only be achieved by strongly reducing the diffraction losses arising at the laser facet. We show here that, somewhat counter-intuitively, opening a carefully designed aperture in a metallic facet coating can simultaneously enhance both its transmission and modal reflectivity by correcting the phase front at the subwavelength scale. Numerical simulations and experimental results demonstrate a reduction of optical mirror loss by up to 40% while the transmission is increased by four orders of magnitude. Applying this approach to both facets of a short cavity quantum cascade laser, we achieve laser operation at room temperature with an electrical dissipation of only 143 mW.

articleTitle: A 27 km over sea surface, 500Mbps, real time wireless communication system at 0.14 THz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 0.14 THz wireless communication system, which can achieve real-time transmission of 30km sea surface with maximum bit rate of 500Mbps, is developed. In the system, the transmitter output power is nearly 2 watts by cascading solid-state power amplifier and vacuum electronic amplifier. A modem with variable transmitting rate is designed from 10Mbps to 500Mbps. An experiment over 27 km sea surface is carried out with two 48 dBi antennas. The feasibility of terahertz wave applied in long range wireless communication and well penetrability through complex and changeable sea surface environment is also demonstrated in this work.

articleTitle: Radial Distortion in Silicon Lens-Integrated THz Cameras
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Silicon lenses are widely employed to turn a terahertz (THz) focal-plane array into a THz camera. For the first time, we have identified the type of radial distortion caused by such lenses. To this end, we measured all single-pixel far-field radiation patterns of a 15-mm diameter 2.75-mm extended hemispherical silicon lens-integrated 32×32-pixel CMOS camera at 0.652 THz. From this, a beam incidence angle grid has been generated, indicating barrel distortion. The measured beam incidence angle is compared to a previously published closed-form relation between scan angle and feed position for extended hemispherical lenses. The presented results are essential for all beam switching applications based on dielectric extended hemispherical lenses with an elliptical extension realized in the lens center.

articleTitle: Improving the Radiation Performance of Resonant-Tunneling Diode by Using Planar Metallic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Resonant-tunneling diodes (RTDs) are promising candidates for terahertz sources but typically exhibit an unexpected large tilt angle in the main lobe of their radiation pattern. In this paper, we present two types of planar metallic arrays, a plasmonic filter and a series-fed patch array, applied to an RTD working at 500 GHz to improve the overall radiation performance. The metallic array is designed through full-wave simulations, and the achieved results for both designs show a large reduction in the main lobe angle. The broadside directivity of the plasmonic filter and the series-fed patch array design reaches 5.4 dBi and 12.5 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Terahertz Topological Waveguide: A Potential Platform for Future Integrated Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a robust topological terahertz planar air-channel waveguide using a simple and innovative low-cost stereolithography 3D printing. Our mechanically reconfigurable waveguide chip supports a wider relative topological bandgap (over 1.6 times) with respect to the only other reported THz topological waveguide, which was based on a silicon-channel. Our work provides a significant step toward THz topological waveguides becoming the physical platform for the next generation of broadband short-range THz wireless communications.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Hydrogen Bond Network of Waters around Polyethylene Glycol by Broadband Dielectric Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Hydration in aqueous polyethylene glycol (PEG) solutions with various molecular weights was evaluated using a broadband dielectric spectroscopy (100 MHz – 18 THz). With the increase of the molecular weight, the restriction strength of hydration waters becomes stronger, while the number of hydration waters decreases. The evaluation results explain an application that the contact lens package solution to employ PEG with low molecular weights.

articleTitle: A THz spectroscopy study of the electrical properties of graphene thin films post-transfer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present terahertz time domain spectroscopy measurements of graphene thin films subject to varying success in the transfer process. The complex conductivity extracted from the time domain measurements gives a clear indication that the quality of the transfer process directly impacts the electrical properties of the graphene. Successfully transferred graphene films show a three-fold improvement of the carrier mobility, as well as a lower scattering rate and carrier density.

articleTitle: Terahertz nondestructive stratigraphic analysis of thick plastic sheets with complex structure
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: SD based on interior point method is used to extract structural information of a sample incorporating both optically thick and thin layers. Pulse spreading is taken into consideration as the THz signal propagates through the thick layers. Compared with both cross-correlation (CC) and frequency wavelet-domain deconvolution (FWDD), the proposed SD algorithm succeeds in resolving the structure of the sample clearly, demonstrating that SD-based approaches might be the preferred option in the presence of both the thick and thin layers.

articleTitle: Sideway terahertz emission from a flowing water line
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We compared the forward and sideway THz wave emission from a flowing water line excited by subpicosecond laser pulses. The peak field of THz sideway emission from a 210 μm waterline in is about twice stronger than that in forward direction when a 2-inch focal length lens is used to focus the optical beam. This observation indicates that the length of plasma in water is much shorter than that in air, resulting in more THz emission to sideway. Moreover, we measured the THz emission energy from water line with different diameters. The forward THz emission decreases greatly when the diameter of the water line increases from 0.3 mm to 1.4 mm. However, the diameter shows a much less influence on the THz emission to sideway, especially for the large diameter of waterline. Our study shows that the sideway detection of THz wave from an ionized waterline is a better scheme to collect more THz signal. These observations are helpful to understand the THz generation from water and laser-induced ionization in water.

articleTitle: Strong coupling of a plasmonic dark mode with photons in a photonic crystal cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We observe strong coupling between the plasmonic dark mode of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) metamaterials with the photons in a 1D photonic crystal cavity in the terahertz frequency range. The observed splitting depends on the strength of magnetic interaction between the plasmon bright-and dark-modes of the EIT metamaterials, demonstrating that the coupling between the dark mode and the cavity photons is mediated by the plasmonic bright mode.

articleTitle: Characterization of stress birefringence of organic silica gel by terahertz time domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The stress optical coefficient of material is an important parameter to measure the internal stress of material by photoelastic method. In this paper, the polarization state terahertz time domain spectroscopy system is built, and the stress birefringence of organic silica gel is measured, so as to obtain the stress optical coefficient in THz region, which provides a basis for the calculation of internal stress. This method verifies the feasibility of the stress optical property law in THz band, and provides a new method for characterizing the internal stress of non transparent materials.

articleTitle: High-harmonic generation from weakly p-doped Si pumped with intense THz pulses
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report high-harmonic generation up to the ninth order from boron-doped Si at room temperature, pumped by intense THz pulses. For comparison with the experiment, we also performed FDTD simulations coupled to a full-band Monte Carlo device model. The simulations predict a significantly stronger flattening of the conversion efficiency with pump power than that observed in the experiments, which points to less pronounced scattering at high fields than expected.

articleTitle: FT-ESR measurements as an application of millimeter wave gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gyrotron is a high-power radiation source in the millimeter and submillimeter wave region, which is suitable for the radiation source of a high frequency (high magnetic field) short-pulsed ESR system. Pulsed ESR spectroscopy system was developed using the high-power millimeter wave of gyrotron. The FID signal of stable radicals of BDPA diluted with polystyrene was successfully observed by the quadrature detection method. By Fourier transforming of these FID signals, high resolution FT-ESR spectrum of BDPA was successfully obtained.

articleTitle: Response Spectrum and Responsivity of Si-based BIB Detector with Varying Anode Bias
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Si-based blocked-impurity-band (BIB) array detector which respond to the wavelength range from 5μm to 50μm has been fabricated. The response spectrum with anode bias scanning from 0V to 3.8V for a single array chip have been measured. Meanwhile, the responsivity and peak responsivity responding to 800K standard blackbody are presented.

articleTitle: THz-TDS Confocal Imaging of Banknote Anti-counterfeiting Labels
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate terahertz imaging of banknote anti-counterfeiting labels by using the THz-TDS confocal imaging system built in our lab. With help of this system, spatial resolution is significantly improved and detail Characters of the anti-counterfeiting labels can be identified. Areas of the multiple overlapping banknotes papers with different number of layers are imaged and distinguished by measuring the time delay and absorption of the THz pulse that transmits through banknotes papers. This technology provides a contactless and nondestructive and high spatial resolution method for screening of banknotes, compared with the conventional THz imaging system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Moisture MApping by Terahertz (MMAT) as a diagnostic test for diabetic foot syndrome
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, the largest THz-imaging study on humans is presented as the first clinical evaluation of a novel technique, named Moisture MApping by Terahertz, for the early diagnosis of the diabetic foot deterioration.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of the Sub-THz Radiation Coupling to n-channel strained-silicon MODFETs
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on a study of the coupling of electromagnetic radiation to a strained-silicon MODFETs used as sub-THz terahertz detector. In particular, the effect of the polarization of the incoming beam as well as the role of the bonding wires on the photoresponse generated were addressed. Two tones were considered: 0.15 and 0.30THz. Results show that the device is sensitive to the beam polarization, especially when the beam polarization is perpendicular to the transistor channel under excitation at 0.15THz. We also demonstrated that the bonding wires play a preponderant role in the coupling of the incoming radiation to the channel of the FET under excitation at 0.15THz while they have a minor role at higher frequencies (0.3THz).

articleTitle: Polarization control of emitted THz waves using spintronic emitters with anisotropic magnetic layers & birefringence characterization of Quartz
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate that spintronic TeraHertz emitters using uni-axial anisotropic FeCo/TbCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/FeCo ferromagnetic layers allow the polarization control of the THz emitted wave thanks to the Stoner-Wohlfarth coherent rotation of magnetization when submitted to a magnetic field along hard axis. The determination of birefringence parameters of a quartz half-wave plate is described as an application example.

articleTitle: Role of Liquid Water in Terahertz Radiation and Application
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) generation and detection using liquid water has long been considered impossible due to its strong absorption of THz wave. A few very recent works reported THz generation from water, but the mechanism has not yet been well clarified and the efficiency demands to be further enhanced. In general, the THz generation and detection are considered as "reversible" theoretical analysis processes. We explore the potential of liquid water as efficient scheme of table-top THz generator and detector. Further underlying physical mechanism, such as the ultrafast electron migration and solvation need to be considered. Moreover, the complex low-frequency molecular motion of water in the THz range has also been successfully identified by the THz Kerr effect technique on the sub-picosecond time scale.

articleTitle: Terahertz modulation of the trion resonance in MoSe2 monolayer
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Here we report a pronounced redshift of the trion resonance in MoSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> monolayer induced by picosecond THz pulses. The kinetic energy gained by hot carriers due to absorption of THz radiation is transferred during the formation of the trion, leading to an effective redshift of its optical transition. By performing time resolved measurements, we have determined the electron cooling time (τ = 70 ps) and estimated the absorption at 7.7 THz (α = 0.3%). A quantitative model based on the Heisenberg equation of motion explains the experimental observations and reproduces the data with good accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved Germanium photoswitch for cavity dumping of a free-electron laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate an optical switch based on gold implanted germanium (Ge:Au) suitable for cavity dumping of a free-electron laser (FEL). We achieve a switching contrast of more than 50 % in a broad range of FEL wavelengths from 6 to 90 µm. A linear relationship between the switching fluence and the frequency of the FEL optical field supported by our simulation highlights the role of a photoinduced finite sub-µm thickness of the reflecting plasma layer. The plasma switch exhibits negligible absorption of the FEL radiation in the ʻoffʼ state and requires only a moderate thermoelectric cooling at incident FEL power of several Watts.

articleTitle: Implementation of Image Information Combining Road Map and Radar Map Image for Autonomous Driving Application
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 79GHz FMCW radar system was developed and radar map image algorithm was realized to detect not only moving objects but also stationary objects around the vehicle at the same time. In particular, the information that detected the curbstones around the road and the navigation map were overlapped, so that the location of the ego-vehicle on the road could be relatively accurate. If GPS signals are not intermittently caught in downtown areas or in low-speed driving, it will be useful to locate autonomous driving vehicles.

articleTitle: Group delay compensation for efficient terahertz generation in two color laser induced air plasma system
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Two-color laser induced air plasma system has been investigated extensively due to its ultrabroadband terahertz spectrum. A zero-order dual wavelength half wave plate is normally used to adjust the polarization of the fundamental wave to enhance the terahertz generation. On top of that, a group delay compensation plate was used to enhance the terahertz generation efficiency further. The influence of second harmonic wave (400nm) for terahertz generation efficiency was also investigated.

articleTitle: Highly efficient and intense terahertz source based on lithium niobate pumped by sub-millijoule ytterbium laser
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have developed a unique THz source combining an average power of 53 mW and maximal field strength of 310 kV/cm. This source is based on lithium niobate crystal pumped by an industrial sub-mJ Ytterbium laser, coupled with an innovative pulse compression technique. Well balanced and highly scalable, this system contributes to democratizing the accessibility of intense and powerful THz pulses.

articleTitle: Dark matter emission from high-power millimeter waves and potential detection by coherent system
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The dark photon, one of the candidates of dark matter, can be generated from high-power millimeter waves. This paper points out possible emission of dark photons from waveguide structures in high-power microwave infrastructure and suggests potential detection of such dark photon signal with a coherent circuit scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a Quasi-Optical Mode Converter for a Dual-Frequency Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Quasi-optical mode converters are usually used in gyrotrons to realize the conversion of high-order cavity mode to Gaussian beam. Using the scalar diffraction theory, the K-S phase-correcting optimization iterative algorithm Geometrical Optics and the least mean square(LMS) algorithm, this paper designs a dual-frequency quasi-optical mode converter with operating frequency of 105 GHz (TE18,7) and 140 GHz (TE24,9). According to the results, the conversion efficiencies are 97.3% at 105 GHz and 99.0% at 140 GHz. And the Gaussian contents of the output beam are 98.0% at 105 GHz and 99.7% at 140 GHz. This dual-frequency quasi-optical mode converter can be used in a dual-frequency gyrotron.

articleTitle: A single-layer terahertz metasurface: from single to an array of sub-wavelength fibers
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the resonances of single, double and array of terahertz sub-wavelength fibers. we demonstrate that the interaction between neighboring elements in the single-layer metasurface (array of fibers) can lead to enhancement or overlap of resonances. The coupling effect between the resonances either diminishes the transmission or eventuates to high transmission compared to single fiber resonances. Such a single-layer metasurface that can operate in both reflection and transmission modes, opens a new avenue to develop single-layer THz devices for wavefront engineering.

articleTitle: Changing the Parameters of Tightly Focused THz Laser Beams
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The possibility for changing the parameters of the focal region of tightly focused laser beams excited by the modes of resonator of a THz laser based on a hollow circular dielectric waveguide was studied theoretically and experimentally. In the experiment, the focusing system was a short-focus lens with the central region covered by absorbing masks. The focal area parameters were changed by varying the size of the masks. The electric field components of the modes under study were theoretically calculated using the integral Rayleigh-Sommerfeld transformations under the non-paraxial approximation. The use of absorbing masks made it possible to reduce the beam diameter in the focal region and increase the depth of focus of the linearly polarized EH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>-mode and azimuthally polarized TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-mode. The results of this work can be implemented in medical diagnostics, high-speed communications, and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Gyrotron Spectrum Control by an External Quasi-Monochromatic Signal with Harmonic or Stepwise (Regular or Random) Modulation of Parameters
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In the present work we compare oscillation regimes in a gyrotron under the influence of a signal with harmonically, stepwise, and randomly varying frequency and amplitude. At stepwise (regular or random) modulation of the signal parameters threshold values of these modulations, corresponding to the excitation of parasitic modes, are lower than at harmonic modulation.

articleTitle: Damage Effect of Devices Induced by High Power Terahertz-wave
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A two-dimensional electro-thermal model of bipolar transistor irradiated by high power terahertz wave is established. The transient behaviors of the bipolar transistor are simulated and analyzed when high power terahertz wave is injected. The damage effect of the electric field, current density and temperature are observed theoretically. The voltage amplitude and the frequency on the device are investigated in detail. Empirical formulas of power damage threshold and energy damage threshold with pulse-width are summarized.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Experiment of a Ka-Band High-Power Output Window
publicationTitle: 2021 46th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, an output window designed for sheet beam travelling wave tube (SB-TWT) with special structure and material is analyzed. The window has a wide bandwidth in Ka-band and simulations show that the reflection coefficient is better than -20 dB within the bandwidth of ~9 GHz (26.2 GHz – 35.2 GHz). The window is designed to operate in continuous wave (CW) state and the power capacity is greater than 12 kW. The output window and the water-cooling system works steadily with 4 kW CW output power at experiment.
